functions.funcName: Provide thrust for all phases of flight
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of generating and controlling propulsive force across all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subName: Provide propulsive thrust from four independent engines
functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans generate thrust independently; inputs: fuel at pump-inlet pressure (from FUE), throttle/reverse commands from flight deck; processing: FADEC dual-channel control; outputs: thrust, engine parameter data to AVI (SDD §5.1.2).

functions.funcName: Provide thrust for all phases of flight
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of generating and controlling propulsive force across all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subName: Provide reverse thrust for ground deceleration
functions.subDef: Two inboard engines produce reverse thrust on the ground; inputs: reverse command, weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement; processing: reverser sleeve deploy with mechanical lock; outputs: reverse thrust. Independence note: reverser deployment inhibited in flight, distinct from forward-thrust path (SDD §5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of positioning aerodynamic surfaces to achieve commanded flight path and attitude across the envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subName: Control aircraft attitude in pitch, roll and yaw
functions.subDef: Position primary surfaces (ailerons/spoilers, stabiliser/elevators, split rudder) to command pitch, roll and yaw; inputs: pilot inceptor, autopilot, air/inertial data from AVI; processing: three dissimilar FBW computers voting; outputs: surface position, envelope-protection status to AVI. Independence note: mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder retained (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of positioning aerodynamic surfaces to achieve commanded flight path and attitude across the envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Extend/retract Fowler flaps and full-span slats to achieve required lift at low speed; inputs: crew/system command; processing: two independent power drive units through common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes; outputs: high-lift position to performance computation. Independence note: common torque shaft is a recorded commonality (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of supporting the aircraft on the ground, absorbing landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and providing braking and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support the aircraft on the ground and provide flotation
functions.subDef: Gear supports the aircraft and spreads footprint pressure to the level semi-prepared surfaces require; inputs: hydraulic A for retract/extend, free-fall alternate; processing: bogie/tyre flotation sizing; outputs: gear position, weight-on-wheels to many consumers. Independence note: free-fall extension independent of hydraulic pressure (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of supporting the aircraft on the ground, absorbing landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and providing braking and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Provide wheel braking to decelerate on the ground
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking decelerates the aircraft within the landing distance requirement; inputs: HYD B normal / HYD A alternate / accumulator emergency, brake commands; processing: electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated, per-wheel-pair anti-skid; outputs: brake temperature to AVI. Independence note: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of supporting the aircraft on the ground, absorbing landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and providing braking and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Provide directional control on the ground by nose-wheel steering
functions.subDef: Steer the nose unit for ground directional control; inputs: tiller and rudder-pedal commands, hydraulic power; processing: hydraulic steering with mechanical disconnect for towing; outputs: nose-wheel angle (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.subName: Provide loading access to the hold
functions.subDef: Open and close the upward-hinging nose visor to allow straight-in loading, and secure it as pressure boundary when closed; inputs: HYD A visor drive plus electric backup, separate lock-actuator supply, pressurisation state from ECS interlock; processing: twelve rotary latches on common torque shaft, eight independent locking pins, dual dissimilar lock sensing; outputs: lock status to flight deck and take-off configuration monitor. Independence note: door structure itself is a single load path treated as STRUCTURE, not authored here (SDD §5.7.2/§5.7.3).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of admitting the blade to the hold and maintaining restraint of a single unitised payload up to 72.6 t through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.7.1, §5.8.1).
functions.subName: Restrain the payload through all load cases
functions.subDef: Position and restrain a single blade on nine saddles; inputs: electrical power to winches, loading plan, weight-on-wheels, nose-door position; processing: two tensioned straps per saddle mechanically locked, continuous tension-monitoring loop; outputs: strap tension and payload distribution to CG computation and restraint status to take-off configuration monitor. Independence note: hold floor hard points have no redundancy and are STRUCTURE; single tension loop is a recorded item (SDD §5.8.2/§5.8.3).

functions.funcName: Condition and pressurise the occupied compartments
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of conditioning and distributing air to the flight deck and hold and controlling the pressure differential across the fuselage (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subName: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold
functions.subDef: Supply conditioned air to the two zones; inputs: engine/APU bleed through cross-bleed manifold, ram air, electrical power; processing: two air-cycle packs, either from either side; outputs: conditioned air, bleed demand to IPS (SDD §5.9.2).

functions.funcName: Condition and pressurise the occupied compartments
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of conditioning and distributing air to the flight deck and hold and controlling the pressure differential across the fuselage (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Maintain flight-deck cabin altitude and low hold differential; inputs: cabin pressure, electrical power, weight-on-wheels, door position; processing: two digital controllers driving two outflow valves plus pneumatic backup; outputs: differential pressure and cabin altitude to AVI and crew-oxygen logic, pressure state to nose-door interlock. Independence note: mechanical relief valves protect structure independently of the control system (SDD §5.9.2).

functions.funcName: Protect the aircraft from ice accretion
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of preventing or removing ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion would be unacceptable, within the icing envelope of the certification basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect wings and engine inlets from ice by bleed heating
functions.subDef: Prevent ice accretion on wing leading edges and inlet cowls; inputs: bleed air from cross-bleed manifold, crew selection; processing: piccolo distribution; outputs: performance penalty applied, bleed demand to ECS (SDD §5.10.2).

functions.funcName: Protect the aircraft from ice accretion
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of preventing or removing ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion would be unacceptable, within the icing envelope of the certification basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect stabilisers, probes and windshields by electrical heating
functions.subDef: Prevent ice accretion on stabiliser leading edges, probes, static ports, windshields and ice detectors; inputs: AC/DC electrical power, TAT and airspeed from AVI; processing: six independently controlled stabiliser zones and individually monitored heated elements; outputs: zone health to AVI, ice-detection advisory to flight deck (SDD §5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of acquiring, processing and presenting the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and hosting the alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Present primary flight, navigation and system information
functions.subDef: Acquire and display flight, navigation and system data; inputs: data from every aircraft system, air/inertial and navigation signals, electrical power; processing: three display processors on dual networks, three reference units, two flight-management computers; outputs: displays to crew, commands to autopilot/autothrottle, recorded parameters. Independence note: standby instrument on DC essential shares no supply, sensor or processing with primaries (SDD §5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of acquiring, processing and presenting the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and hosting the alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Consolidate system status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures; inputs: status from every system; processing: two independent processing channels; outputs: prioritised alerts and procedures to crew (SDD §5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of detecting fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and providing the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subName: Detect fire, overheat and smoke in monitored zones
functions.subDef: Detect fire/overheat in nacelles, APU, bleed-duct runs and gear bays, and smoke in the hold; inputs: DC essential power, weight-on-wheels, APU state; processing: dual continuous loops with AND logic degrading to single-loop, nine hold smoke stations; outputs: fire/overheat and smoke warnings to crew alerting (SDD §5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of detecting fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and providing the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subName: Extinguish fire in engine and APU zones
functions.subDef: Discharge extinguishing agent into nacelles and APU compartment; inputs: hot-battery-bus power to discharge circuits, crew fire-handle commands, APU state; processing: two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair, dedicated APU bottle with automatic discharge unattended; outputs: discharge status, automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation. Independence note: hold has detection but no suppression by recorded decision (SDD §5.12.2/§5.12.3).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of supplying breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and the subsequent descent and diversion (SDD §5.13.1).
functions.subName: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew on demand
functions.subDef: Supply oxygen to four mask stations for the required diversion duration; inputs: two HP cylinders on a crossover manifold, cabin-altitude signal from ECS, crew donning action, DC power for indication only; processing: demand regulators independent per mask; outputs: oxygen to masks, cylinder pressure and low-pressure alerting to flight deck. Independence note: no automatic deployment; no passenger oxygen as hold is unoccupied in flight (SDD §5.13.2).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines with no crew command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust change produces an unrequested longitudinal and, if asymmetric across the 28 m outboard moment arm, directional/rolling upset requiring immediate crew correction; at take-off/low altitude an uncommanded increase or asymmetric loss challenges the directional-control sizing case.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded change and counter with rudder/thrust-lever action; workload is high in the take-off/landing phases where margins are smallest.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded asymmetric thrust change across the outboard 28 m moment arm at low speed challenges directional control (the SDD's sizing case) and significantly raises crew workload; proposed Hazardous pending FCS directional-control authority substantiation — a worst-case near-ground upset could argue Catastrophic and needs the sizing analysis to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to a crew thrust command
fha.effAc: Engine(s) deliver thrust different from that commanded (wrong magnitude or wrong engine responding), producing a longitudinal and potentially asymmetric response inconsistent with crew intent; at take-off or on the approach the mismatch can defeat the crew's expected trajectory correction.
fha.effCrew: Crew commands thrust and receives an unexpected result, must diagnose and re-command; increased workload and potential for control mistrust in critical phases.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous response to command in a critical phase can produce an asymmetric or wrong-direction thrust that challenges the directional-control sizing case and materially raises workload; proposed Hazardous pending confirmation against the FCS/FADEC command-integrity and rudder-authority analysis. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow thrust drift below the crew detection threshold
fha.effCrew: By definition undetected; crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect of a slow undetected drift is not established by the function definition alone — whether the drift produces controllable asymmetry, fuel/range penalty, or converges to a hazardous divergence depends on drift magnitude and rate, which are undefined in the provided material. Severity left empty pending the drift-bound and asymmetry-onset analysis; not classifiable as No Safety Effect without it.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of propulsive thrust with resulting directional-control asymmetry within control authority
fha.effAc: Loss of thrust on one engine produces an asymmetric yawing/rolling moment across the 28 m moment arm; within the design case the aircraft continues to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine at or after V1, with the required rudder authority holding the asymmetry.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply rudder to counter asymmetry, identify and secure the affected engine (fuel shut-off/fire handle), and manage a continued-flight/diversion; elevated but manageable workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-engine loss is within the design dispatch case — continue to a suitable aerodrome with directional control retained — a significant reduction in capability and increased crew workload, supporting Major; confirm against the engine-out handling and performance case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of propulsive thrust with asymmetry beyond available directional-control authority
fha.effAc: Thrust loss producing asymmetry exceeding rudder authority (e.g. loss of a second engine on the same side, outside the design dispatch case) yields a yawing/rolling moment the crew cannot fully counter, threatening loss of directional control at low speed.
fha.effCrew: Crew have insufficient control authority to hold heading/wings-level; the condition exceeds the retained-authority assumption and may not be recoverable near the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetry beyond directional-control authority at low speed threatens loss of control of the aircraft; the SDD identifies same-side second-engine loss as outside the design dispatch case and retained for study, which is consistent with a Catastrophic potential outcome. Proposed Catastrophic pending the directional-control authority boundary analysis that defines when asymmetry actually exceeds authority. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation (all four engines)
fha.effAc: Aircraft can no longer sustain powered flight; forced descent to a glide/off-airport landing with no thrust available on any of the four independent engines.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an unpowered forced landing with high workload and no recovery of thrust; outcome depends on altitude and available landing site.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; only flight crew (nominal two, up to four) exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of all propulsive thrust removes the ability to sustain flight in every phase; per AC 25.1309-1B the worst-case phase drives a Catastrophic classification (safety objective Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded reverse thrust deployment in flight (inboard engine)
fha.effAc: In-flight deployment of an inboard reverser produces asymmetric thrust and drag against the in-flight inhibit; potential loss of control depending on phase and speed.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter a sudden asymmetric thrust/drag event with rudder and thrust management; high workload with limited time margin at low altitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; only flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects are stated but the aircraft-level outcome depends on whether the described in-flight inhibit (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) is defeated and on the residual controllability under asymmetric inboard reverse, which the function definition does not establish; severity cannot be derived without that controllability determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on ground deceleration (one inboard reverser)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric reverse from one of the two inboard reversers produces a yawing moment during the ground deceleration roll, degrading directional control on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter the yaw with steering and differential braking during rollout on an unimproved strip; workload elevated within the deceleration margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; only flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The directional-control outcome depends on how much of the deceleration margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout) and steering/braking authority remains under asymmetric reverse on a semi-prepared surface; the function definition does not quantify the controllable range, so severity cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground deceleration thrust (reverse thrust)
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust contribution lengthens the deceleration distance; wheel braking on a semi-prepared surface must absorb more of the stop within the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply increased braking and monitor rollout margin on the unimproved strip; workload elevated but a deceleration means remains available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; only flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reverse thrust is a supplementary decelerator and wheel braking remains available, but whether partial loss keeps the stop within the 1,800 m requirement on a semi-prepared surface is not established by the function definition; severity cannot be derived without the braking-only stopping-distance case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground deceleration thrust (reverse thrust)
fha.effAc: No reverse thrust available; the ground stop relies entirely on wheel braking (system B normal, A alternate, plus accumulator reserve) within the deceleration margin on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew decelerate on wheel braking alone; workload elevated on an unimproved strip and rollout margin reduced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; only flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Wheel braking remains the primary deceleration means (SF-006), so the aircraft-level effect turns on whether braking alone stops the aircraft within the 1,800 m requirement; the function definition does not establish the braking-only performance, so severity cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of reverse thrust unannunciated at deceleration onset
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: reverse thrust is a ground-deceleration contributor only (reversers on the two inboard engines), but the SDD does not state the reverse-thrust share of the landing stopping budget versus wheel braking, so the aircraft effect of its unannunciated loss on the 1,800 m requirement vs 1,080 m predicted rollout cannot be stated. Needs the deceleration-budget decomposition to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous attitude response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft attitude departs from the commanded state in pitch, roll or yaw; erroneous response to inceptor input threatens the ability to control aircraft trajectory and maintain controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew commands do not produce the intended attitude response; crew must detect the discrepancy and attempt recovery through degraded/reversion paths, high workload.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed for confirmation. SF-003 is aircraft attitude control feeding 'control aircraft trajectory'; an erroneous attitude response to crew command at this level is a loss of the ability to control the flight path and can prevent continued safe flight and landing. Effects-driven, not preconceived. Confirm against the FCS reversion argument (mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and lower rudder only). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded attitude motion with no command
fha.effAc: Aircraft attitude changes in pitch, roll or yaw with no crew or autopilot command; uncommanded motion drives the aircraft away from the intended flight path and threatens controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise an unexpected attitude excursion, arrest it and re-establish the intended state, high workload; recovery depends on remaining control authority.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed for confirmation. An uncommanded attitude excursion at the aircraft-trajectory level can develop into an unrecoverable departure and prevent continued safe flight and landing. Effects-driven. Confirm severity and any crediting of envelope protection / reversion. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow uncommanded attitude divergence below crew threshold
fha.effAc: Aircraft attitude diverges slowly in an uncommanded manner below the threshold at which the crew or displays flag it; the aircraft drifts from the intended flight path and the discrepancy grows before it is recognised.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no corrective action; by the time the divergence becomes apparent the excursion is larger and recovery margin is reduced.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed for confirmation — engineering judgement. Because the divergence is undetected the crew take no action (per the unaware assumption), so a slow attitude drift degrades trajectory control and reduces recovery margin. Whether this reaches Catastrophic depends on the divergence rate vs the recovery envelope, which the SDD does not quantify. Confirm rate/envelope before fixing severity. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous attitude response below crew threshold
fha.effAc: Aircraft attitude responds erroneously to command at a magnitude below the crew/display detection threshold; the flight path is progressively established away from the intended state without the crew being aware.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue to command normally and take no corrective action; the accumulated trajectory error is not recognised until it exceeds the detection threshold, reducing available recovery margin.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed for confirmation — engineering judgement. Undetected erroneous attitude response (crew take no action) degrades trajectory control and erodes recovery margin; the ceiling between Hazardous and Catastrophic depends on the error magnitude and how long it accumulates before threshold crossing, which the SDD does not quantify. Confirm against the detection-threshold and recovery analysis. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of attitude control authority within controllable limits
fha.effAc: Reduced control authority in one or more axes; aircraft remains controllable within a reduced envelope with increased crew workload; degraded control law annunciated.
fha.effCrew: Crew flies in a degraded law with envelope protection reduced or lost; increased workload; must respect a restricted manoeuvre envelope.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in safety margins and control authority with a large increase in crew workload, but aircraft remains controllable within limits — Hazardous (Severe-Major) per §25.1309, objective 1e-7/fh, for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of attitude control authority beyond controllable limits
fha.effAc: Remaining control authority insufficient to maintain controlled flight in the affected axis; loss of ability to keep the aircraft within a controllable envelope.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest divergence with remaining authority regardless of workload; controlled flight not maintainable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of control beyond the controllable limits prevents continued safe flight and landing — Catastrophic per §25.1309, objective 1e-9/fh, derived from stated effects, for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of attitude control authority
fha.effAc: No means of controlling aircraft attitude in the affected axes; aircraft attitude uncontrolled.
fha.effCrew: Crew has no effective means to control attitude; controlled flight cannot be maintained.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of the primary trajectory-control function prevents continued safe flight and landing — Catastrophic per §25.1309, objective 1e-9/fh, derived from stated effects, for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment
fha.effAc: Left/right high-lift mismatch generates a rolling moment and lift asymmetry; asymmetry brakes arrest the affected drive but the aircraft holds a locked asymmetric configuration requiring lateral control to counter.
fha.effCrew: Crew counters the rolling moment with lateral control at increased workload; must fly an approach and landing in an asymmetric high-lift configuration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on the aircraft is a controllable roll asymmetry per the SDD's asymmetry-brake description, but the SDD does not state the magnitude of the resulting rolling moment or whether it remains within lateral control authority in the take-off/landing case; without that the severity (Hazardous vs Catastrophic if uncontrollable) cannot be derived — needs FCS/handling data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces move without command, producing a lift/drag and pitch-trim change and a configuration inconsistent with the flight phase; effect and controllability depend on airspeed and direction of movement.
fha.effCrew: Crew responds to an unexpected configuration change and out-of-schedule performance; workload and severity depend on flight phase and airspeed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD describes high-lift architecture and asymmetry brakes but does not characterise the aircraft-level effect of an uncommanded symmetric high-lift movement (e.g. overspeed/structural exceedance if extended above limit speed, or lift loss if retracted at low speed); the effect magnitude and worst phase are not grounded, so severity cannot be derived — needs FCS high-lift schedule and limit-speed data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift capability (flaps/slats unavailable) for low-speed flight
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot achieve the reduced stall/approach speeds high-lift provides; take-off and landing performed at substantially increased speeds and distances, with the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout no longer assured.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload flying a high-speed approach and landing; go-around and diversion assessment required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the high-lift on which the semi-prepared landing distance margin rests degrades take-off/landing performance and safe speed margins; on effects a large reduction in safety margin with high crew workload at low speed — proposed Hazardous, engineer to confirm whether effects reach Catastrophic at the semi-prepared strip. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of high-lift capability (reduced flap/slat availability) for low-speed flight
fha.effAc: Reduced high-lift authority raises take-off and landing speeds and distances by a lesser amount than total loss; performance margin against the 1,800 m landing requirement is eroded but not eliminated.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload; reference-speed and landing-distance reassessment for the degraded configuration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced high-lift is a significant reduction in performance margin with increased crew workload short of the total-loss case; proposed Major, engineer to confirm against the actual degraded-configuration performance data. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected asymmetric high-lift below the detection threshold
fha.effAc: An asymmetry in flap/slat deployment not annunciated to the crew produces an uncommanded rolling/yawing moment at low speed; magnitude depends on the asymmetry the threshold permits before the asymmetry brakes act.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action regarding the asymmetry; they continue normal duties and counter any resulting roll as a handling anomaly of unknown cause.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft effect depends on how much asymmetry the sub-threshold band permits and on the asymmetry-brake/detection performance, which the function definition does not state. Need the asymmetry detection threshold and the resulting roll/yaw authority impact at low speed to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous indication of ground support/flotation configuration (indicated state does not match true gear/configuration state)
fha.effAc: Misleading configuration indication may lead the crew to believe the aircraft is correctly configured for ground contact when it is not, or vice-versa; consequence at aircraft level depends on the true configuration masked by the erroneous indication.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on false configuration information; the take-off/landing configuration check is corrupted, potentially driving an incorrect landing decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft effect turns on WHICH true state the erroneous indication conceals (e.g. gear not down/locked shown as locked at touchdown). The function definition and SDD do not fix that true state, so no single effect drives a severity — need the specific masked configuration and phase.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ground support configuration integrity (gear/flotation not correctly configured, with no indication to the crew)
fha.effAc: The aircraft contacts the surface without the ground-support configuration required to absorb landing/taxi loads and provide flotation on a semi-prepared strip, with no warning; potential gear collapse or loss of ground support.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no corrective action; continue the landing normally.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without the specific true failure state and phase: an undetected not-down-and-locked gear at touchdown vs a degraded flotation margin on taxi produce very different effects. Need the configuration-integrity failure defined and the flotation/structural-load consequence stated before deriving severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support capability — reduced load-carrying/footprint capability on the ground with the aircraft still supported on its gear
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains supported but ground support capability is degraded; footprint pressure or load-spreading is reduced, which on the semi-prepared destination strip may cause rutting, bogging or loss of controlled ground handling.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage a degraded ground roll/taxi; workload and directional-control demand increase on an unmaintained surface.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD establishes semi-prepared operation and flotation as a sizing basis, but does not quantify the aircraft-level consequence of PARTIAL loss (which bogies/how much footprint reduction, at what weight/surface). Cannot ground a §25.1309 aircraft effect severe enough to classify without that partial-degradation case — left empty pending engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of adequate flotation on a semi-prepared surface — footprint pressure exceeds what the operating surface can bear while the gear remains structurally intact
fha.effAc: On the semi-prepared destination strip the tyre/footprint no longer floats on the surface; gear penetrates, ruts or bogs, risking loss of directional control, an excursion, or the aircraft becoming immobilised during the landing rollout or taxi within the 1,800 m distance.
fha.effCrew: Crew face degraded or lost ground directional control and stopping performance on an unmaintained surface with no line maintenance at the strip.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD gives flotation as a sizing basis for the semi-prepared surface but no aircraft-level outcome for its loss (excursion vs immobilisation, speed, whether structural collapse follows). NOTE: this condition is not currently in the SF-005 FCIM — reconcile before classifying. Severity left empty pending the flotation-loss consequence and confirmation the condition belongs to SF-005.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support and flotation capability — the aircraft cannot be supported on the ground by any means (e.g. gear collapse / no support at touchdown)
fha.effAc: Aircraft is not supported at or after touchdown; loss of controlled ground contact leads to structural contact with the surface, likely airframe damage and an uncontrolled ground path, on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot arrest or control the aircraft on the ground by any means once support is lost.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point to a severe outcome, but the SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of total loss of ground support (survivability of an unsupported touchdown, structural collapse behaviour, occupant/crew injury). Cannot derive Catastrophic vs Hazardous from the description alone — left empty for engineering confirmation rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Braking erroneously applied against crew command — wheel braking responds incorrectly to, or opposite, the crew's braking command
fha.effAc: Erroneous braking (asymmetric or against command) during the ground roll degrades or destroys directional control and stopping predictability; on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout this can produce an excursion or overrun, with tyre/gear overload from asymmetric braking.
fha.effCrew: Crew command is not honoured; crew must detect and counter erroneous braking while maintaining directional control on an unmaintained surface, increasing workload sharply at a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD gives the stopping margin (1,800 m vs ~1,080 m) and dual/accumulator braking, but does not quantify the aircraft-level effect of erroneous/asymmetric braking (excursion probability, controllability, whether the margin is consumed). Cannot derive Major vs Hazardous without that controllability/performance case — left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground wheel-braking deceleration
fha.effAc: No wheel-braking deceleration available; on the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout the stopping margin is lost, giving high likelihood of overrun/excursion beyond the prepared surface. Inboard reverse thrust and accumulator-reserve emergency braking (six applications) partially mitigate but do not restore full authority on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: High workload managing an overrun/excursion; crew reverts to reverse thrust and accumulator emergency braking.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers or payload occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of braking against a landing-distance requirement with little margin on an unprepared surface can lead to a high-energy runway excursion; proposed Catastrophic for engineer confirmation. Depends on the credit taken for reverse thrust and accumulator emergency braking, which the FHA does not model. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced braking with degraded stopping performance
fha.effAc: Braking still available at reduced effectiveness; stopping distance increases and erodes the ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout. On a nominal-friction prepared portion the margin absorbs moderate degradation; on the semi-prepared strip a larger degradation risks overrun. Inboard reverse thrust supplements deceleration.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload; crew applies maximum braking and reverse thrust and monitors remaining distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Degraded but symmetric braking against the stated ~720 m rollout margin, with reverse thrust available, is a significant reduction in safety margin rather than an excursion in the nominal case; proposed Major for engineer confirmation. The point at which residual margin is exhausted, and worst-case surface friction, are not given. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking across the wheel groups
fha.effAc: Differential braking left-to-right across the main bogie groups produces a yawing moment and directional deviation during the ground roll. On a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip a directional deviation risks lateral departure from the surface; nose-wheel steering and rudder counter the yaw within their authority.
fha.effCrew: High workload maintaining runway track against the induced yaw using steering and rudder while decelerating.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided material gives the function and the landing case but not the magnitude of asymmetry (which wheel groups, how much differential torque) nor the available steering/rudder counter-authority on a low-friction surface, so the resulting directional deviation — and thus the aircraft effect — cannot be quantified from the inputs. Severity left empty pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded braking effectiveness below crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Small reduction in braking effectiveness that the crew does not detect; the crew continues the deceleration normally and takes no compensating action. Because the degradation is below the detection threshold it is bounded to a small stopping-distance increase absorbed by the ~720 m rollout margin under nominal conditions.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continues duties normally, no additional action taken.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: By definition the degradation is below the crew-detection threshold and therefore small, absorbed by the stated rollout margin under nominal friction; proposed Minor for engineer confirmation. Assumes the sub-threshold amount cannot combine with an adverse (semi-prepared, low-friction) surface to exhaust the margin — not established by the inputs. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Anti-skid regulation error not evident to the crew
fha.effAc: Anti-skid regulates braking incorrectly (over- or under-releasing) without crew awareness; the crew continues normal braking. Effect on stopping distance and directional control depends on the regulation error magnitude and the surface friction, neither of which is given.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the regulation error; continues normal braking with no compensating action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition establishes per-wheel-pair anti-skid but not the magnitude or direction of an undetected regulation error, nor its effect on stopping distance or track on the semi-prepared surface. Without a stated aircraft effect the condition cannot be classified; severity left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Nose-wheel steering erroneously responds to a crew command (erroneous directional response) — ground
fha.effAc: Erroneous steering response produces a directional deviation not matching crew intent during ground roll; on a semi-prepared strip with limited lateral margin this can lead to lateral runway/strip excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives deviation and must correct with rudder pedals, differential braking and reverse; increased workload during a high-speed ground phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Ground directional deviation could range from a correctable event to a strip excursion depending on speed, achievable crew correction and lateral margin on the semi-prepared surface; the provided material does not quantify controllability or excursion outcome, so severity cannot be derived. Fill after ground-handling/controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose-wheel deflection with no crew command — ground
fha.effAc: An uncommanded deflection introduces a directional disturbance the crew did not command during ground roll; on a narrow semi-prepared strip this can drive a lateral excursion if not corrected in time.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the unexpected yaw/heading change and counter it with pedals and differential braking; startle and correction workload highest at high ground speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Outcome spans a correctable disturbance to a runway/strip departure; magnitude and rate of the uncommanded deflection, and the crew's ability to arrest it within the strip's lateral margin, are not characterised in the provided material, so severity cannot be derived. Fill after controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Small uncommanded nose-wheel steering bias not evident to the crew — ground
fha.effAc: A small undetected steering bias produces a slow directional drift during ground roll; on the semi-prepared strip this consumes lateral margin over the roll distance.
fha.effCrew: Crew are unaware of the bias and continue normal duties; correction, if any, is only via the residual heading cues they act on, so the drift is opposed later and less completely than an announced fault.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Whether a sub-detection bias merely raises crew tracking effort or accumulates into a strip excursion over the roll depends on bias magnitude and available lateral margin, neither quantified in the provided material; severity cannot be derived. Fill after ground-handling assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority or range (partial loss of directional control on the ground)
fha.effAc: Reduced steering authority degrades the aircraft's ability to hold and correct ground track, particularly at low speed and during turns; alternative directional means (rudder at speed, differential braking, reverse on inboard engines) remain available.
fha.effCrew: Crew must supplement with rudder and differential braking; taxi and turn manoeuvring on the semi-prepared strip is slower and higher-workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced (not lost) steering authority with rudder and differential-braking directional means still available is a degradation of ground directional capability that raises crew workload and reduces margin; consistent with a Major failure condition. Confirm against the strip lateral margin and available alternate directional authority. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric or restricted directional response of nose-wheel steering (partial loss)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric or restricted response gives unequal turn capability or limited travel, biasing achievable ground track and complicating tracking on a narrow strip; other directional means remain available.
fha.effCrew: Crew compensates with pedals, differential braking and reverse and adapts turn technique; increased workload during ground manoeuvring.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect ranges from a manageable manoeuvring restriction to a directional-control degradation at speed depending on the degree of asymmetry/restriction and the available lateral margin; the provided material does not quantify these, so severity cannot be derived. Fill after ground-handling/controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded nose-wheel steering response below the crew-detection threshold (partial loss, crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Reduced ground directional-control precision; small tracking errors on the ground the crew does not detect and does not correct. On a semi-prepared 1,800 m strip with ~1,080 m predicted rollout, margin exists but lateral tracking is degraded.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation; crew continue normally with a subtly degraded steering response, correcting via rudder/differential braking as available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the SDD gives the steering purpose (§5.6.1) and the strip/rollout margins (§1.1) but does not quantify how much tracking degradation is tolerable on the semi-prepared surface, nor the availability of rudder/differential-braking compensation at low speed. Need the directional-control budget to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering directional control (crew aware)
fha.effAc: No steering from tiller/pedals; ground directional control must be maintained by rudder aerodynamic authority and differential braking (§5.6.2 steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals). At high ground speed on a semi-prepared strip, lateral control authority and available runway margin become limiting; low-speed taxi manoeuvring is severely restricted.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated/apparent as no steering response; crew revert to rudder and differential braking, and may need to reject or curtail the ground manoeuvre.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot firmly classify: the SDD states steering commands come from tillers AND rudder pedals (§5.6.2) and that rudder is sized for the engine-out directional case (§5.1.3/§5.3.3), but does not establish whether rudder plus differential braking retains adequate directional control at high ground speed on the semi-prepared surface without steering. That determines whether this is Major or Hazardous. Directional-control-on-loss-of-steering analysis needed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Nose cargo door indicated locked to the crew when not fully secured (erroneous indication, crew unaware)
fha.effAc: The visor forms the pressure boundary and part of the forward-fuselage structural load path when closed (§5.7.1). An indicated-locked-but-unsecured door defeats the take-off configuration check (§5.7.6) and can permit in-flight opening/loss of the pressure boundary and load path with pressurisation applied.
fha.effCrew: Crew dispatch and pressurise believing the door secured; no cue until a structural/pressure event develops.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. In-flight loss of a pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage primary load-path element (§5.7.1) with no crew cue (indication defeated, take-off config check defeated per §5.7.6) is a plausible loss-of-aircraft outcome. Confirm the structural/pressurisation consequence of an unlatched visor in flight and the effectiveness of the dual dissimilar sensing being defeated in this specific mode. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Nose cargo door indicated open to the crew when actually secured (spurious open indication)
fha.effAc: Door is in fact secured and the pressure boundary/load path intact; the false indication is misleading only. Door cannot be operated in flight (§5.7.6), so no erroneous in-flight opening can result from the indication.
fha.effCrew: Spurious 'door not locked' cue; crew may reject a take-off or divert unnecessarily, and must resolve a lock-status disagreement between the two dissimilar sensing paths (§5.7.2).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the aircraft effect turns on crew response to a spurious cue (rejected take-off dynamics on the semi-prepared strip, or unnecessary diversion), which the SDD does not characterise. Also note this condition is not currently in the SF-008 FCIM; confirm it should be carried before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Incomplete nose cargo door lock engagement not detected by either sensing path (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical-linkage indicator, §5.7.2) fail to reveal incomplete pin engagement, so the visor pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path (§5.7.1) are compromised without any crew cue and pressurisation is applied.
fha.effCrew: Crew have no lock-status disagreement and no cue; they dispatch and pressurise believing the door fully secured.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Defeat of BOTH dissimilar sensing paths leaving a pressure-boundary/primary-load-path element incompletely locked with no crew cue is a plausible in-flight loss-of-aircraft outcome. Confirm the structural/pressurisation consequence of incomplete pin engagement and treat the common defeat of both dissimilar paths as an independence claim to be tested (§5.7.2/§5.7.5). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded or slowed loading/unloading access to the hold
fha.effAc: Loading/unloading proceeds at reduced rate or with degraded access; no in-flight effect — the door cannot be operated in flight and the hold is unoccupied.
fha.effCrew: Ground crew experience slowed loading; extended turnaround; no flight-crew action in flight.
fha.effPax: None — hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Ground-only condition per SDD §5.7.6 'cannot be operated in flight' and §5.8.6 'Loading is a ground procedure'; effect is turnaround delay/dispatch operability, no flight-safety nexus. Proposed Minor for engineer confirmation; if treated purely as an operability/schedule item it may be No Safety Effect at aircraft level — confirm the intended classification convention. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of hold loading/unloading access
fha.effAc: Payload cannot be loaded or unloaded; aircraft cannot be dispatched with cargo or unloaded on arrival; no in-flight effect.
fha.effCrew: Ground crew cannot complete the loading procedure; no flight-crew action in flight.
fha.effPax: None — hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Ground-only condition per SDD §5.7.6/§5.8.6; complete loss of access prevents mission but has no in-flight aircraft/crew safety effect. Proposed Minor for confirmation; may be an operability/No Safety Effect item under the programme's classification convention — confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded restraint at one or more stations, within remaining capability, annunciated to the crew
fha.effAc: Restraint at a station reduced but blade remains restrained; per §5.8.3 loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours; condition annunciated in flight, loss on two adjacent stations flagged as requiring immediate attention.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to strap tension loss / restraint condition; assumed to divert or apply reduced-manoeuvre procedure as required.
fha.effPax: None — hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Degraded but not lost restraint on a 72.6 t blade, annunciated, with load carried by neighbouring straps per §5.8.3; crew aware and can act. Proposed Major on the basis that a further single failure could progress toward blade movement; confirm — the aircraft-level effect of the residual degraded state is not fully stated in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Restraint status erroneously indicated intact when restraint is degraded (crew unaware of degraded restraint)
fha.effAc: Blade restraint degraded while indication shows intact; crew continue normally and take no action; a degraded restraint on a 72.6 t single blade progressing to movement would affect longitudinal CG and structural load path — the aircraft-level outcome is not stated in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware, take no restraint action; misleading indication removes the opportunity to divert or manage the condition.
fha.effPax: None — hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class: the SDD describes restraint architecture and monitoring but does not state the aircraft-level consequence (CG excursion magnitude, controllability, structural outcome) of an undetected in-flight degradation/movement of the 72.6 t blade. Classifying would require an assumption about the CG/structural effect of blade movement, which is engineering judgement not in the document. Left empty pending that input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of longitudinal restraint tension at a single strap station, with the blade otherwise restrained
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One of two straps at one saddle station loses tension; SDD states load paths are sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so blade position and centre-of-gravity are maintained. Condition is annunciated to the crew via the tension monitoring loop.
fha.effCrew: Restraint condition annunciated; crew monitor, no in-flight adjustment available, dispatch/continuation decision. Increased attention.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect. Crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Neighbouring straps carry the lost strap (SDD 5.8.3), restraint of the 72.6 t blade is maintained and the condition is annunciated; effect is a slight increase in crew workload with no reduction in aircraft capability — Minor. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Restraint degradation at a station outside the tension-monitoring-loop coverage, undetected by the crew
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Restraint degradation occurs where the single instrumented tension loop does not provide coverage, so it is not annunciated; crew continue normally taking no action. Undetected progressive loss of restraint on a 72.6 t single blade could permit blade shift under load cases, adversely affecting centre-of-gravity and controllability. Actual extent of uncovered stations and worst-case shift are not stated in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; no indication of the degradation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect. Crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD records the tension loop as a single instrumented loop whose coverage is a recorded item but does not state which stations are outside coverage, nor the resulting worst-case blade shift and its effect on controllability; the aircraft effect cannot be grounded, so severity is left empty pending the restraint-coverage and blade-shift analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload restraint of the single blade through the flight and ground load cases
fha.effAc: Total loss of longitudinal restraint of a single unitised blade of up to 72.6 t occupying the full 108 m hold; uncontrolled shift of the blade under flight load cases produces large centre-of-gravity excursion and can defeat controllability and structural integrity. On the ground/at rotation the shift is a loss-of-control precursor.
fha.effCrew: Restraint loss annunciated; crew have indication only, no in-flight restraint adjustment; unable to arrest a shifting 72.6 t blade.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect. Crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncontrolled shift of a 72.6 t single blade over the full 108 m hold produces a centre-of-gravity excursion and loading no crew action can arrest (indication only, no in-flight adjustment), plausibly resulting in loss of control — Catastrophic. Confirm against the CG/controllability substantiation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous conditioning or pressurisation control response — the ECS drives conditioning or differential opposite to or in excess of demand
fha.effAc: Erroneous pressurisation control can drive the fuselage differential the wrong way or beyond schedule; independent positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure regardless of the control system, and either outflow valve is sufficient. Erroneous flight-deck conditioning affects the occupied compartment; hold is unoccupied. Crew become aware via cabin-altitude/differential indication to the avionics and can select the manual/pneumatic backup mode.
fha.effCrew: Erroneous differential/cabin-altitude annunciated; crew select manual pressurisation or pneumatic backup and don oxygen if required; increased workload and possible diversion.
fha.effPax: Occupied compartment is the flight deck only (crew); hold unoccupied — no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Structure is protected by independent mechanical relief and either outflow valve is sufficient, and the crew have indication plus a manual/pneumatic backup mode; an erroneous control response therefore yields a significant increase in crew workload and possible diversion rather than an unrecoverable condition — proposed Major. Confirm against the crew-oxygen/cabin-altitude effect and the FL260 differential. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressure-differential control developing below the crew detection threshold, crew unaware and taking no action
fha.effAc: Slow erroneous drift of the fuselage differential below the crew detection/annunciation threshold; crew continue normally and take no action. Independent mechanical relief protects the structure at the limit, but a slow cabin-altitude drift toward the ~8,800 m hold-equivalent could reach a physiological threshold before annunciation. The differential schedule and hold altitude equivalent are preliminary/unfrozen, so the worst-case unannunciated cabin altitude and time-to-threshold are not stated.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; slow drift below threshold means no timely donning of oxygen; hold unoccupied.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect. Crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The hold pressurisation differential (~8,800 m equivalent) is preliminary and not frozen, and the SDD does not state the crew detection/annunciation threshold or the worst-case unannunciated cabin altitude reached before mechanical relief acts; the physiological aircraft effect on the crew cannot be grounded, so severity is left empty pending the pressurisation-schedule and crew-oxygen timing analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced air conditioning/distribution capacity or single-zone loss to occupied compartment
fha.effAc: Degraded conditioning to flight deck and/or hold; single-pack operation permitted with reduced hold conditioning schedule, aircraft continues.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage reduced conditioning; alternate pack/bleed selection available; increased crew attention.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-pack operation is explicitly permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule, and the hold is unoccupied; flight-deck conditioning degradation with the crew acting is a slight reduction in functional capability — proposed Minor for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow loss of pressurisation differential below crew-detection threshold (unaware)
fha.effAc: Gradual reduction in fuselage differential below the design schedule; hold altitude equivalent rises toward/beyond the low-differential design point.
fha.effCrew: Crew assumed unaware and take no action; flight-deck cabin altitude may rise slowly toward crew oxygen thresholds.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The flight deck is held at a conventional cabin altitude and crew oxygen exists, but the SDD does not state the flight-deck cabin-altitude excursion or physiological outcome resulting from a slow, undetected differential loss; cannot derive whether crew incapacitation risk arises. Severity left empty pending the cabin-altitude/time effect data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution to occupied compartments
fha.effAc: Loss of conditioned-air supply and distribution to the flight deck; pressurisation depends on conditioning air source, potential loss of flight-deck environmental control.
fha.effCrew: Crew lose flight-deck conditioning; if pressurisation cannot be maintained, descent and crew oxygen use required; workload increases significantly.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Two independent packs from four bleed sources exist, so total loss requires multiple failures, but the SDD does not state the flight-deck cabin-altitude/temperature consequence of a total conditioning loss nor the diversion outcome; the aircraft-level effect cannot be bounded. Severity left empty pending the flight-deck environmental effect and required-descent data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous over-pressurisation of the occupied compartment
fha.effAc: Erroneous differential-control drives fuselage above schedule; independent positive-pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to abnormal differential; select manual pressurisation mode; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Independent positive/negative mechanical relief protects the structure regardless of the control system, and the hold is unoccupied; however the SDD does not state the flight-deck occupant effect (ear/physiological or structural margin) if relief functions as intended, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be classified. Severity left empty pending the relief-protected differential margin and flight-deck occupant effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pressure differential control
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential no longer controlled; cabin/hold altitude follows ambient. Independent mechanical relief still protects the structure against over/under-pressure, but no active differential is maintained.
fha.effCrew: Flight deck cabin altitude rises toward ambient; crew must don oxygen and initiate emergency descent to a safe altitude. Increased workload during descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried, so no occupant depressurisation effect beyond the flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on the maximum cabin/flight-deck altitude reached and time-to-incapacitation once differential is lost, against crew oxygen availability and descent capability from FL260. The SDD gives max operating altitude FL260 and a preliminary hold differential (~8,800 m equivalent) but does not state flight-deck cabin altitude on total loss or the resulting altitude-exposure profile; without that, the effect on the crew cannot be bounded and severity cannot be derived. Confirm flight-deck depressurisation profile and crew-oxygen diversion adequacy.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced control of pressure differential
fha.effAc: Differential still controlled but at reduced capability or with degraded schedule; single-outflow-valve or reduced-authority operation.
fha.effCrew: Crew has indication of degraded pressurisation control and may need to select manual mode or limit altitude. Increased monitoring workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — To classify a partial loss, the aircraft effect must be bounded by how far differential can deviate under 'reduced control' and whether crew action returns it to an acceptable schedule. The SDD states two controllers, two outflow valves 'either valve being sufficient', and a pneumatic backup, but does not quantify the residual differential excursion or cabin altitude under reduced control; without a bounded effect, severity cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic control with manual reversion available
fha.effAc: Automatic pressurisation control lost; pneumatic backup mode drives one outflow valve directly on cabin pressure. Differential still maintained by manual/backup means.
fha.effCrew: Crew reverts to manual/pneumatic backup control of pressurisation; increased workload to schedule differential manually but a safe cabin altitude remains achievable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on the aircraft is 'manual reversion available' with a pneumatic backup driving one outflow valve on cabin pressure; classifying requires knowing whether the backup holds an acceptable cabin altitude and the crew-workload/attention impact of manual scheduling. The SDD confirms the backup mode exists but does not state the resulting cabin-altitude adequacy or the crew workload, so severity is not yet derivable.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous under-pressurisation of the occupied compartment
fha.effAc: Control drives the fuselage to a lower-than-scheduled differential; occupied (flight-deck) compartment altitude higher than intended. Negative relief protects structure but does not restore differential.
fha.effCrew: Flight-deck cabin altitude rises above schedule; if it exceeds physiological thresholds the crew must don oxygen and descend. Detection depends on cabin-altitude alerting.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; occupied-compartment effect is limited to the flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on how high the flight-deck cabin altitude rises under erroneous under-pressurisation and whether it is annunciated in time for crew oxygen/descent. The SDD provides FL260 max altitude and the preliminary hold differential but not the flight-deck cabin-altitude excursion under this malfunction nor the cabin-altitude warning threshold; the effect cannot be bounded, so severity is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressure differential schedule developing below detection thresholds
fha.effAc: Differential follows an erroneous schedule that develops slowly and below crew-detection thresholds; deviation accumulates without annunciation until it becomes significant.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties and takes no action (unaware condition); protection reduces to the automatic detection and independent relief. Erroneous schedule may reach a hazardous cabin altitude or over-pressure before it is detected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; occupied-compartment effect limited to the flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is the crew-unaware malfunction: with no crew action, the driving question is the worst cabin-altitude or over/under-pressure the erroneous schedule can reach before the independent relief or any residual alerting intervenes. The SDD confirms independent mechanical relief and cabin-altitude sensing but does not quantify the detection threshold or the worst undetected excursion; without that bound the effect and severity cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous activation of bleed-air ice protection (wings/engine inlets) when not required, reducing available capacity
fha.effAc: Uncommanded bleed demand reduces engine bleed available to the ECS packs and imposes a thrust/performance penalty when not needed; the SDD notes wing anti-ice in use reduces pack capacity and applies a performance penalty.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe the erroneous activation and displayed performance penalty; can deselect. Effect if unaware left to the paired condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: SDD §5.10 states the bleed demand reduces pack capacity and imposes a performance penalty but does not quantify the aircraft-level consequence (available-thrust margin, ECS/pressurisation impact) that would drive severity. Needs the performance/ECS margin analysis to derive class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of bleed-air ice protection on protected aerodynamic surfaces and engine inlets
fha.effAc: Reduced or lost anti-ice on part of the wing leading edge or an engine inlet cowl in the icing envelope; residual capacity remains and a lost element is annunciated. Aircraft-level handling/thrust consequence not stated in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: A lost bleed sector would be annunciated; crew action (exit icing, select manual) available but the aircraft-level effect of the degraded surface/inlet is not stated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: SDD §5.10 defines the function and its redundancy but does not state the aircraft effect of a partially-iced protected surface or inlet (stall-margin/handling degradation, inlet ice-shed/engine effect). The icing-envelope aero and engine assessment is required to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of bleed-air ice protection on a protected surface or engine inlet
fha.effAc: With no annunciation, ice accretes unchecked on an unprotected surface or inlet while the crew continue normally; the aircraft-level consequence of that accretion is not stated in the SDD but is worse than the annunciated case because no crew mitigation occurs.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action regarding the loss, continuing in the icing envelope on the assumption protection is available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: undetected accretion on a protected surface/inlet is where 'where accretion would be unacceptable' bites, but the SDD does not state the resulting aircraft-level handling, stall-margin or engine consequence needed to derive severity. Requires the icing aero/engine analysis and detection-coverage assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of bleed-air ice protection on protected aerodynamic surfaces and engine inlets
fha.effAc: No anti-ice available to wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls in the icing envelope; unchecked accretion on surfaces and inlets where the SDD states accretion 'would be unacceptable'. The aircraft-level handling/thrust/engine consequence is not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Bleed protection is available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold, so complete loss implies loss of that manifold source; crew would exit icing if able. Detailed crew mitigation and its adequacy not established.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the SDD alone: total loss of protection on surfaces/inlets 'where accretion would be unacceptable' points to a severe class, but the SDD does not state the aircraft-level effect (stall-margin loss, controllability, inlet/engine effect) or the availability of exit-from-icing, which are needed to derive the class. Requires the icing-envelope aero and engine assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous electrical heating activation (stabilisers/probes/windshields) when not required, reducing available electrical capacity
fha.effAc: Uncommanded electrical heating load draws electrical capacity when not needed; the SDD describes the electrical elements as individually monitored and independently supplied but does not state the aircraft-level effect of the erroneous electrical draw on other essential loads.
fha.effCrew: Erroneous activation would be visible via zone health/status; crew can select manual/deselect. Aircraft effect if unaware not stated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: SDD §5.10/§5.13 do not quantify the electrical-capacity consequence of an erroneous heating draw (whether it can compromise essential-bus loads under a generation-limited case). The electrical load analysis is required to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of electrical ice protection across heated zones and elements (stabilisers, probes, ports, windshields)
fha.effAc: One or more of six independently supplied stabiliser zones, or individually monitored probes/ports/windshields, lose heating; remaining zones/elements continue to protect. Lost zone is annunciated. Localised ice accretion possible on the affected surface or sensor within the icing envelope.
fha.effCrew: Zone-loss annunciation presented; crew apply icing procedure and may restrict operation in the icing envelope. Affected probe/port heating loss cross-checked against redundant sensing.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition and SDD establish that a lost electrical zone is annunciated and that heating is independently supplied in six zones with individually monitored probes, but the aircraft-level effect of a single degraded zone or element within the icing envelope (handling/sensor consequence) is not quantified by the function definition alone. Cannot derive severity without the icing-envelope effect on remaining margin; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of heating on an individually monitored probe, port or element
