fha.effAc: Heating lost on a monitored probe, static port or element with NO annunciation; ice accretes on the affected sensor within the icing envelope, producing erroneous or frozen air-data (airspeed, altitude, angle-of-attack) or degraded windshield vision, with no fault cue to the crew.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally taking no action, as the loss is undetected; they may act on corrupted air-data feeding displays and protections, or lose forward vision.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With the loss undetected the crew act on potentially erroneous air-data; the effect could be severe. But the aircraft-level consequence depends on whether the corrupted sensor is voted out by the three ADIRUs / standby instrument (an architecture claim in the SDD, not in the function definition) — I cannot derive severity from the function definition alone without that integrity/voting argument. Left empty per abstention rather than assume the severe or benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of electrical ice protection on stabilisers, probes and windshield
fha.effAc: All electrically heated protection lost: all six stabiliser zones, all probes/static ports, ice detectors and windshields unheated. In the icing envelope, ice accretes on the horizontal/vertical stabiliser leading edges, on air-data sensors (degrading airspeed/altitude/AoA), and on windshields (loss of forward vision) simultaneously. Bleed protection to wings/cowls is unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Multiple annunciations of lost electrical zones/elements; crew must exit the icing envelope, manage degraded air-data and degraded vision, and divert. High workload in icing conditions.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Simultaneous loss of stabiliser anti-ice, air-data sensor heating and windshield heat in the icing envelope is plausibly Hazardous or worse, but classifying it requires the effect on the aircraft within the certification icing envelope (handling/air-data margin), which the function definition does not state. Left empty per abstention; do not reach for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading primary flight information
fha.effAc: Primary flight information (attitude, airspeed, altitude) presented to the crew is erroneous with NO fault cue. Crew fly the aircraft on false primary references, potentially commanding the aircraft outside its intended trajectory or envelope with no immediate means to detect the error.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally, taking no corrective action, and act on the misleading information; recovery depends on an independent cross-check (standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing) being consulted and believed in time.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Undetected misleading primary flight information means the crew fly on false attitude/airspeed/altitude with no cue; on a transport-category aircraft this failure condition is classically Catastrophic because it can lead to loss of control before the error is recognised. The independent standby instrument (SDD: shares no supply, sensor or processing) is a mitigation to be credited in the SFHA/PSSA, not at aircraft-function level. Confirm against the AVI integrity architecture; if credited independence downgrades the exposure the class may reduce. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading primary flight, navigation and system information presented to the crew (crew unaware, continue normal duties)
fha.effAc: Aircraft flown on erroneous flight/navigation data the crew believes is valid; no standby cross-check triggered because the fault is undetected. Potential departure from intended trajectory, terrain/obstacle proximity or loss of control before any recovery is attempted.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on misleading information as if correct; no annunciation prompts reversion to the independent standby instrument; error is not caught until physical cues diverge, if at all.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from the stated effect: undetected misleading primary information acted upon by an unaware crew, with the standby cross-check not triggered, can drive an unrecoverable trajectory/loss-of-control outcome. Confirm against worst applicable phase (low-visibility approach/landing). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary flight, navigation and system information (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Reduced primary display or reference capability; remaining display processors and reference units continue to present valid information, with the independent standby instrument available as backup.
fha.effCrew: Crew are annunciated of the degradation, reconfigure displays (reversionary selection is manual) and continue using remaining primary and standby sources; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the aircraft-level outcome depends on HOW MUCH primary information is lost and in which phase (a single display processor loss versus loss of two of three reference units differ). SDD confirms residual capability but not the worst-case partial extent — needs the safety derivation to bound the remaining-capability case per phase.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary flight, navigation and system information with independent standby information available (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Primary displays lost; the independent integrated standby instrument, sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, continues to provide standby attitude, airspeed and altitude, permitting continued flight and landing at degraded capability.
fha.effCrew: Crew revert to the standby instrument (manual reversion), fly on standby attitude/airspeed/altitude, and conduct a diversion/landing at increased workload with reduced situational information.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the aircraft-level severity of continuing to fly and land on standby-only information depends on the phase, workload and the visibility/approach case — the SDD substantiates that standby capability exists and is independent, but does not establish the worst-phase outcome. Needs the safety derivation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary flight, navigation and system information (crew aware)
fha.effAc: All primary display and reference presentation lost; the independent standby instrument remains the only source of attitude, airspeed and altitude, with no primary navigation or system information available.
fha.effCrew: Crew reduced to the standby instrument only; substantially increased workload; navigation and system-status information unavailable, degrading the ability to manage the aircraft and complete a safe diversion, particularly in IMC.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the outcome hinges on the worst applicable phase (e.g. loss in IMC on approach versus VMC cruise) and on the adequacy of standby-only flight/landing — the SDD substantiates residual standby capability but does not establish the worst-phase aircraft effect. Needs the safety derivation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous alert presented to the crew (crew aware)
fha.effAc: A false or incorrect alert is presented; crew may respond to a non-existent condition or be distracted from a real one, with potential for an inappropriate configuration or trajectory change.
fha.effCrew: Crew are presented a false/incorrect alert, must diagnose it against other information, and may take an unnecessary action or divert attention; increased workload and potential for a wrong response.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: severity depends on WHICH alert is erroneous and the crew action it induces (a spurious warning driving an inappropriate response in a critical phase differs greatly from a nuisance caution). The SDD confirms dual independent alerting channels but does not bound the worst erroneous-alert content — needs the safety derivation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Crew alert presented with incorrect priority (mis-prioritisation of a valid alert against other concurrent alerting)
fha.effAc: An existing condition is annunciated but ranked incorrectly against concurrent alerts; the aircraft state is unchanged but the crew's attention and procedure selection may be misdirected, delaying response to the more critical condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew may action a lower-priority condition first or overlook the higher-priority one; increased workload and potential for a delayed or incorrect response.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on which conditions are mis-ranked and the time-criticality of the delayed response, which the aircraft-function definition ('consolidate and present crew alerting') does not by itself bound; worst-case downstream severity requires the SFHA/PSSA to establish the set of alerts affected and the consequence of delayed action. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to present a crew alert for an existing condition (required alert not presented while the condition is present)
fha.effAc: A real system condition exists but is not annunciated to the crew; the aircraft continues in a degraded or hazardous state with no alerting-driven crew response, so the condition can progress unmitigated.
fha.effCrew: Crew remain unaware of the condition and continue duties normally, taking no corrective or protective action; the safety benefit of the alerting-driven procedure is lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unaware omission of an alert removes the crew mitigation for whatever underlying condition existed; the resulting aircraft effect is bounded by the most safety-critical condition whose alert can be omitted, which the aircraft-function definition does not enumerate. Worst-case severity requires the SFHA/PSSA to identify the set of alerts and the hazard each mitigates. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected suppression or omission of a required crew alert (alert silently suppressed with no indication that alerting is incomplete)
fha.effAc: A required alert is suppressed and the crew have no indication that the alerting function is incomplete; the aircraft can be in a degraded or hazardous state with the crew falsely assured that no alert exists.
fha.effCrew: Crew rely on the absence of an alert as evidence of a normal state and take no action; false assurance defeats the crew mitigation and can persist until the underlying condition manifests by other means.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected suppression removes both the alert and any cue that the alerting is degraded, so the effect is bounded by the most safety-critical suppressible alert; the aircraft-function definition does not enumerate which alerts can be silently suppressed, and worst-case severity requires the SFHA/PSSA to establish the integrity/coverage of the alerting channels. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew alerting consolidation and presentation (some alerts or alerting capability lost, remainder available)
fha.effAc: A subset of alerting is unavailable; some conditions are still annunciated while others are not, and the crew's overall situational picture and procedure selection are degraded but not eliminated.
fha.effCrew: Crew have reduced alerting coverage; for the affected conditions they receive no annunciation and take no alerting-driven action, with increased workload to monitor unalerted systems by other means.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on which portion of alerting is lost and the criticality of the unalerted conditions; the aircraft-function definition ('consolidate and present crew alerting') does not bound which alerts are in the lost partition. Worst-case severity requires the SFHA/PSSA to establish the coverage lost. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting consolidation and presentation (no consolidated crew alerting available)
fha.effAc: No consolidated alerting is presented; the aircraft may enter or remain in any failed or hazardous state with no automatic annunciation, and the single prioritised crew alert path that tells the crew what has failed and what to do is unavailable.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no consolidated alerting for any condition and must detect and diagnose all failures by direct system indication and airmanship; substantial increase in workload and high potential for delayed or missed response to a concurrent safety-critical condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss of the consolidated alerting path removes crew mitigation across all conditions simultaneously; the aircraft-level effect is bounded by the worst concurrent condition the crew would fail to detect, which the aircraft-function definition does not enumerate and which depends on the integrity/independence of the two alerting channels. Worst-case severity requires the SFHA/PSSA to establish residual crew detection means. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: False fire, overheat or smoke warning presented with no actual event
fha.effAc: Unwarranted crew response to a non-existent fire: potential unnecessary engine shutdown / extinguishant discharge and diversion; aircraft otherwise fully serviceable.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload and distraction; crew executes fire/shutdown drill for a phantom event, degrading available thrust/systems by their own action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false warning driving an unnecessary in-flight engine shutdown/discharge reduces available margin and significantly increases crew workload but leaves the aircraft controllable with remaining engines — consistent with Major. PROPOSED; confirm whether crew response could credibly cascade to a worse outcome (e.g. shutdown of a good engine on the same side as a failed one). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate a genuine detected fire, overheat or smoke event
fha.effAc: An actual fire/overheat progresses without crew warning; extinguishing (a crew action via fire handles) is not initiated, allowing an uncontained nacelle/APU/bleed/gear-bay fire to develop.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the event, take no protective action; first indication may be secondary effects (thrust loss, structural/system damage).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of warning for a genuine fire defeats the sole means by which the crew initiates suppression, permitting an unannunciated fire to progress in a fire zone (engine/APU) or a flammable-fluid wing region; an undetected progressing fire is potentially Catastrophic. PROPOSED — confirm against the fire-zone containment case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire/overheat/smoke detection in one or more monitored zones
fha.effAc: Detection coverage lost in the affected zone(s) — a fire/overheat in that zone would be unwarned and unsuppressed; other zones remain protected.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated (per dual-loop degradation logic where applicable); crew aware coverage is reduced but has no warning for an event in the affected zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect depends on WHICH zone loses coverage — loss of an engine-nacelle or APU fire-zone loop is far more severe than loss of a single hold smoke station. The condition as stated spans a range of zones; a single severity cannot be grounded without specifying the affected zone. Left blank; recommend splitting by zone (fire zone vs hold smoke) before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat coverage
fha.effAc: Overheat detection on the bleed-duct runs and main gear bays lost; a bleed-air leak/overheat or a gear-bay/brake overheat would progress unwarned, risking duct/structure damage or a gear-bay fire from hot brakes.
fha.effCrew: No overheat warning for the affected runs/bays; crew cannot take isolating action (e.g. bleed shut-off) in time.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on the consequence of an undetected bleed-duct overheat (duct/structure/pressure-boundary damage) and an undetected gear-bay overheat (brake/tyre fire) — the SDD identifies these as overheat-monitored zones but does not characterise the resulting hazard progression. Severity not derivable from the description alone; left blank pending the overheat-consequence assessment for each zone.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of smoke detection along the hold (detection unavailable, crew aware of the fault annunciation)
fha.effAc: Loss of the sole means of detecting a smoke event in the unoccupied hold; the hold has smoke detection at nine stations and no suppression fitted, so a developing hold fire could progress undetected with no protection.
fha.effCrew: Crew are annunciated the detection loss but have no in-flight means to inspect or suppress in the hold; diversion is the available response.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect severity from the SDD alone: the consequence of an undetected hold fire depends on the flammability/threat of the single-blade payload and on the un-substantiated 'no hold suppression' decision, neither of which the SDD classifies. Effects stated; classification withheld pending payload fire-threat and the recorded suppression assumption being substantiated.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of a hold detection loop below the warning threshold (crew unaware; detection coverage silently reduced)
fha.effAc: Detection capability is silently reduced with no fault annunciation; a smoke event in a partially-uncovered region of the unoccupied hold could go undetected while the crew believe detection is intact.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties taking no action; no cue that coverage is degraded.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Same gap as the aware case, aggravated by the loss of the fault annunciation: severity of an undetected hold fire depends on the payload fire-threat and the un-substantiated no-suppression decision, which the SDD does not classify. Effects stated; classification withheld.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire, overheat and smoke detection (engine nacelles, APU, bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat, and hold smoke)
fha.effAc: Simultaneous loss of detection across all monitored fire/overheat zones — the four engine nacelles, the APU compartment, the bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat coverage, and the hold. A fire or overheat in any monitored zone could develop and progress with no warning to initiate extinguishing (which is a crew action through the fire handles).
fha.effCrew: No fire/overheat/smoke annunciation available; crew cannot detect the condition that triggers the extinguishing action, and would not know to discharge.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed for engineer confirmation. Total loss of detection across engine nacelle and APU fire zones removes the trigger for extinguishing; an undetected engine/APU fire in a high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone can propagate to loss of the aircraft. Effects drive Catastrophic per AC 25.1309-1B; confirm against the extinguishing dependency and phase set. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge with no fire (unwanted discharge into an engine or APU zone)
fha.effAc: One extinguisher bottle is expended with no fire present; with two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed, remaining agent for a genuine event in that pair is reduced. No direct loss of a flight function from the discharge itself.
fha.effCrew: Crew see discharge status; a subsequent genuine fire in the affected pair has reduced available agent.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects stated but severity not derivable from the SDD alone: the aircraft-level consequence hinges on whether a single inadvertent discharge alone (agent expended, no fire) produces a hazardous condition or merely reduces reserve for a later event. The SDD gives the two-bottle cross-plumbed architecture but does not state the effect of an in-flight inadvertent discharge on the affected engine. Classification withheld pending that effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to discharge extinguishant on crew command (fire present, extinguishing unavailable in an engine or APU zone)
fha.effAc: With a detected fire in an engine nacelle or the APU compartment, the crew command through the fire handle produces no discharge; the sole means to extinguish that fire is unavailable and the fire can progress in a high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew have detected and annunciated the fire and initiated the extinguishing action but it does not take effect; no alternative in-flight suppression exists for that zone.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed for engineer confirmation. Inability to extinguish a detected engine/APU fire in a designated fire zone (high energy, flammable fluid) can lead to uncontained fire and loss of the aircraft; effects drive Catastrophic per AC 25.1309-1B. Confirm the credit taken for shut-off/fuel-isolation and cross-plumbing before freezing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced fire extinguishing capability in a protected engine or APU zone (degraded agent availability across the protected zones)
fha.effAc: Reduced probability of successful fire suppression in a protected zone should an engine or APU fire occur; a fire that would otherwise have been extinguished may continue, with the second cross-plumbed bottle of the affected engine pair possibly still available.
fha.effCrew: Crew fire drill executed with reduced likelihood of extinguishing success; increased workload managing a potentially continuing fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level effect for a REDUCED (not total) extinguishing capacity: the SDD gives cross-plumbed dual bottles per engine pair but does not state the consequence of a fire continuing with degraded agent, and severity depends on the coupled fire/uncontained-fire case not provided here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire extinguishing to one engine or APU zone only (that protected zone unable to receive agent on demand)
fha.effAc: An engine or APU fire in the affected zone cannot be extinguished by the fixed system; fire may continue and progress in that zone until the source is isolated by shutdown and fuel/APU isolation.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute engine/APU fire drill (shut-off, fuel isolation, fire handle) but fixed extinguishing is unavailable for that zone; increased workload and diversion decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on whether an unsuppressed single-zone fire remains contained after engine/APU shutdown and fuel isolation — the SDD describes the isolation means but does not state the aircraft-level outcome of a continuing fire, so the effect cannot be classified from provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of agent charge before demand — a protected zone's extinguishing agent unavailable at the moment of demand with no prior crew awareness
fha.effAc: On occurrence of an engine or APU fire, the fixed extinguishing attempt fails because agent is already depleted; the crew discover the loss only at the moment it is needed.
fha.effCrew: Crew initiate fire drill expecting extinguishing and receive no discharge effect; no prior indication was available to plan around the deficiency.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Latent (undetected) loss combined with a fire at demand is a coupled condition; the SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an unsuppressed engine/APU fire, so the effect chain cannot be closed and severity cannot be derived here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fixed fire extinguishing in engine and APU zones (no protected zone can receive agent on demand)
fha.effAc: No engine or APU fire can be extinguished by the fixed system; any such fire must be managed by shutdown and fuel/APU isolation alone, and may continue and progress with potential for structural or systems damage in the affected zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew fire drill provides source isolation only; no fixed extinguishing available for any engine or APU zone; diversion required with elevated workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The worst-case outcome depends on whether an unsuppressed engine/APU fire can be contained by isolation alone — an uncontained fire case not established in the SDD; severity cannot be derived without that aircraft-level effect and the coupled fire/PRA analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or contaminated breathing oxygen delivered to the flight crew on demand
fha.effAc: Effect on the aircraft is mediated through crew performance; the SDD does not state an aircraft-level chain for contaminated crew oxygen.
fha.effCrew: Flight crew (nominal two, provision for four) receive erroneous or contaminated oxygen when donning masks for a depressurisation, smoke or fume event, potentially degrading or incapacitating crew at the moment supplemental oxygen is required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried; no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect is entirely through crew incapacitation during the very event that demands oxygen; the SDD describes the system and its use but gives no aircraft-effect chain or crew-performance-to-outcome linkage, so severity cannot be derived from provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to deliver oxygen to the crew on donning action (system does not respond to demand when masks are donned)
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; the aircraft remains controllable.
fha.effCrew: Crew don masks in a depressurisation, smoke or fume event and receive no oxygen; onset of hypoxia/incapacitation at the prevailing altitude, degrading ability to conduct the emergency descent and diversion. Failure only manifests at the moment of demand.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED — no oxygen at the moment of demand during a depressurisation/smoke event drives the crew toward incapacitation with a reduced ability to fly the emergency descent and diversion; effect is on flight crew only (hold unoccupied). Time-to-incapacitation against the diversion time at FL260 is not quantified in the SDD — confirm against sizing before accepting. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of delivered oxygen quality (contaminated or off-specification oxygen delivered to the crew)
fha.effCrew: Crew breathe degraded/contaminated oxygen believing supply is adequate; potential impairment of crew performance. The condition is undetected, so the crew take no corrective action.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD describes indication of cylinder pressure and system status but does not describe monitoring of delivered oxygen quality, nor the physiological effect or time-course of the contaminant. Aircraft effect and the degree of crew impairment cannot be grounded — need the oxygen quality/contamination monitoring capability and physiological data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen availability to the crew (degraded supply capacity or reduced reserve)
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; the aircraft remains controllable.
fha.effCrew: Reduced oxygen reserve available to the crew; supply may be insufficient for the full diversion time at the maximum operating altitude, with low-pressure alerting. Crew aware via continuous cylinder-pressure indication and can manage the descent/diversion accordingly.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without quantifying remaining availability against the required diversion time. SDD states the system is sized for four occupants for the diversion time with reserve and that a single cylinder can supply at reduced reserve — whether a 'reduced availability' still covers the required duration is not stated. Need the reserve margin / duration data to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen supply to a single mask station (one of four demand-regulated mask stations without oxygen)
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; the aircraft remains controllable.
fha.effCrew: One mask station without oxygen; the affected crew member is without breathing supply at that station in a depressurisation/smoke event. Nominal complement is two crew of four mask stations, so a remaining donning position is available; regulators are independent per mask, isolating the failure to one station.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: severity depends on which/how many crew positions are occupied at the time and whether the affected crew member can relocate to an available station. SDD gives a nominal complement of two with four mask stations and independent per-mask regulators, but does not state the operational assumption for crew relocation. Need that operational assumption to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of breathing oxygen supply to the crew (no oxygen available at any mask station)
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; the aircraft remains controllable by other means.
fha.effCrew: No breathing oxygen available to the flight crew for a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event or the subsequent descent and diversion; crew face hypoxia/impairment at the prevailing altitude with no oxygen to support the emergency descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED — total loss of the crew oxygen supply removes the protection intended for depressurisation/smoke/fume events and the following diversion; drives the crew toward incapacitation and materially reduces ability to conduct the descent and diversion. Effect is on flight crew only (hold unoccupied). Time-to-incapacitation at FL260 against diversion time is not quantified in the SDD — confirm whether the emergency-descent-to-survivable-altitude margin supports Hazardous rather than a more severe class. — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The ten function-consuming systems (PRP, FCS, LDG, NZD, CRG, ECS, IPS, AVI, FPR, OXY) map to aircraft-level behaviours, while FUE, HYD, EPS and EWS are resources not authored as functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly declines to state the aircraft-level function list (Appendix A), forcing derivation of the function/resource split from the §2.1 Type column and the modelling rule.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a resource system carries an aircraft behaviour not reducible to supply (e.g. FUE managing CG/wing-bending), a function is missing and the decomposition is incomplete.
assumptions.usedFor: The set of top functions authored; the exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: The nose visor structural load path and the hold floor hard points are STRUCTURE, substantiated by structural analysis and PRA, not functional-FHA items.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD identifies both as single load paths with no redundancy, but does not classify; the modelling rule requires structure be excluded from functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If either is to be carried as a functional item, an additional function/FC is needed rather than a PRA-only treatment.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion notes on the NZD access and CRG restraint sub-functions.

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: Engine-out continuation and directional control after loss of one engine are treated as attributes of the thrust and trajectory-control functions rather than as a separate top-level function at this decomposition pass.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD frames engine-out continuation and the asymmetric-thrust sizing case as design conditions across PRP and FCS, not as a named function; whether to split is an engineering-judgement call left to the engineer.
assumptions.ifWrong: A distinct 'continue safe flight after loss of any one engine' aircraft function would be added, changing the function list and its downstream AFHA rows.
assumptions.usedFor: The 'Provide thrust' and 'Control aircraft trajectory' function scoping; offered as a choice.

citations.quote: The aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is a continuous ground-deceleration action, so its malfunction set includes uncommanded in-flight deployment and asymmetric application.
assumptions.rationale: The function list names reverse thrust for ground deceleration but not the in-flight inhibit; the SDD supplies it.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-002 malfunction entries and the in-flight-deployment condition would be removed or reworded.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002 malfunctions[] (uncommanded reverse thrust deployment in flight)

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.text: SF-005 combines ground support and semi-prepared-surface flotation, so total loss and flotation shortfall are distinct partial conditions.
assumptions.rationale: The function text pairs 'support on the ground' with 'provide flotation'; splitting is needed to avoid hiding a condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-005 partials[] split into support-loss vs flotation-loss would collapse into a single partial.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005 partials[] (partial loss of ground support / loss of adequate flotation)

citations.quote: spreads footprint pressure to the level the operating surfaces require, and provides braking

assumptions.text: Thrust and attitude complete-loss conditions warrant a within-controllable-limits vs beyond-controllable-limits partial split because directional/control authority is a sizing case.
assumptions.rationale: The function list alone gives only the capability; the SDD grounds asymmetry/authority as the driving margin.
assumptions.ifWrong: The two-partial (within/outside controllable) modelling on SF-001 and SF-003 would revert to a single degraded partial.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 partials[], SF-003 partials[]

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: Crew-indication and mitigation detail cannot be grounded at aircraft-function level from the SDD, so those fields are left empty.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes system-level alerting but the FHA effects/detection means for these aircraft functions do not yet exist.
assumptions.ifWrong: Detection/mitigation fields would be populated and some Unaware rows could be dismissed.
assumptions.usedFor: detection and mitigation fields on all SF-001..SF-005 rows

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list

assumptions.text: SF-006 and SF-007 failure conditions manifest on the ground with weight-on-wheels available, so ground-phase detection cues apply.
assumptions.rationale: The function list names ground braking/steering but does not state the flight phase or detection cues; grounding awareness requires the operating phase.
assumptions.ifWrong: If some conditions manifest in other phases the awareness split and indication rows for SF-006/SF-007 change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 and SF-007 Aware/Unaware rows

citations.quote: weight-on-wheels and wheel speed to the avionics

assumptions.text: Some braking/anti-skid degradation and steering bias can develop below crew-detection thresholds, justifying a crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not state detection coverage limits for anti-skid or steering, so the undetectable-degradation split is inferred, not grounded.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all such degradation is annunciated the SF-006/SF-007 Unaware rows collapse into the Aware rows.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 and SF-007 Unaware rows

citations.quote: Anti-skid operates per wheel pair.

assumptions.text: SF-009 restraint degradation outside the single tension loop's coverage can go unannunciated, supporting a crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD flags loop coverage as a recorded open item rather than confirming full coverage, so undetected degradation cannot be excluded.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loop coverage is complete the SF-009 Unaware row is not applicable.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-009 Unaware row

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item.

assumptions.text: SF-008 door lock-state misindication (indicated secure while not fully engaged) is credible because the SDD carries dual sensing as an integrity provision rather than proving misindication impossible.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes two dissimilar sensing paths but does not quantify their coverage of partial engagement, so a misindication malfunction is retained.
assumptions.ifWrong: If dual sensing fully precludes misindication the SF-008 malfunction and Unaware rows change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008 malfunction entries and Unaware row

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.text: An erroneous pressurisation schedule can drift within displayed cabin-altitude/differential indication before crossing a crew alerting threshold, justifying the SF-011 Unaware malfunction row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states differential/cabin altitude is sent to avionics and crew oxygen logic but does not define the alerting threshold, so the sub-threshold undetectable band is assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any pressurisation deviation is immediately annunciated, the SF-011 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011 Unaware malfunction row

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.text: Ice detection is advisory only, so a loss of protection on a protected surface can remain crew-unaware if no dedicated protection-failure annunciation covers that surface.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD annunciates lost electrical zones and states detection is advisory, but does not confirm every bleed-protected surface has a coverage annunciation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If every protected surface has a dedicated loss annunciation, the SF-012 Unaware partial row collapses into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012 Unaware partial-loss row

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available

assumptions.text: Misleading primary/navigation/system information from the display chain can be presented without self-evident cue, warranting the SF-014 Unaware malfunction rows.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes redundant processing and a comparison-independent standby but does not establish that all erroneous-data cases are detected and annunciated in real time.
assumptions.ifWrong: If cross-comparison always detects and flags misleading data, the SF-014 Unaware rows collapse into detected (Aware) conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-014 Unaware malfunction rows

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus

assumptions.text: The alerting system can fail to raise a required alert without itself annunciating that omission, justifying the SF-015 Unaware malfunction rows.
assumptions.rationale: Dual independent processing channels are stated but no self-monitor for alert omission is described in the provided sections.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a monitor detects and annunciates missing alerts, the SF-015 Unaware rows collapse into detected conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015 Unaware malfunction rows

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: The crew-Unaware detection row for SF-016 is warranted because a detection-path failure can persist below warning threshold with no self-annunciation.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual-loop AND-to-single-loop degradation but does not state whether loop health is annunciated, so the undetectable case cannot be dismissed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loop failure is always annunciated, the SF-016 Unaware row collapses and only the Aware row remains.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016 Unaware row (undetected detection-loop degradation / silent detection loss)

citations.quote: AND logic between them for warning, degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen degradation is at least partly annunciated because cylinder pressure is displayed continuously and low-pressure alerting is provided.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives continuous pressure indication and low-pressure alerting but does not address delivered-oxygen quality monitoring.
assumptions.ifWrong: If quality is monitored, the SF-018 Unaware oxygen-quality row collapses; if pressure indication is unreliable, the Aware split for quantity loss weakens.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018 Aware quantity rows and SF-018 Unaware oxygen-quality row

citations.quote: cylinder pressure and system status to the flight deck; low pressure alerting

assumptions.text: Engine/APU extinguishing agent state may not be continuously monitored, so an undetected charge-loss partial for SF-017 is retained pending confirmation.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes discharge status output but does not state whether pre-demand agent charge is continuously indicated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If agent charge is continuously monitored and alerted, the SF-017 Unaware row is deleted.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017 Unaware row (undetected loss of agent charge before demand)

citations.quote: Out: Fire and overheat warnings to the crew alerting system; discharge status

assumptions.text: For a single-engine partial thrust loss the retained rudder authority holds the resulting asymmetry within control limits, making SF-001-PL a controllable (Major) condition rather than a loss-of-control event.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the aircraft is designed to continue after loss of any one engine and that the rudder authority requirement is carried in the flight-control sizing, but the provided material does not quantify the retained margin.
assumptions.ifWrong: If retained authority is insufficient for the single-engine case, SF-001-PL severity rises from Major toward Hazardous/Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-PL severity (Major)

citations.quote: the resulting rudder authority requirement is carried in the flight-control sizing

assumptions.text: An uncommanded or erroneous asymmetric thrust event at low speed can develop asymmetry approaching the directional-control sizing case, driving SF-001-M and SF-001-M2 to Hazardous.
assumptions.rationale: The moment-arm sizing case is stated qualitatively; the provided material does not bound the magnitude or rate of an uncommanded/erroneous thrust excursion, so its worst-case asymmetry is assumed to approach the sizing case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If uncommanded/erroneous excursions are bounded well below the sizing asymmetry, SF-001-M and SF-001-M2 could reduce to Major; if they can exceed authority near the ground they could rise to Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-M severity (Hazardous), SF-001-M2 severity (Hazardous)

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: Same-side second-engine loss (or equivalent asymmetry) represents the case where asymmetry exceeds directional-control authority for SF-001-PL2.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names same-side second-engine loss as outside the design dispatch case and retained for study, but does not confirm it is the asymmetry-beyond-authority boundary.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the beyond-authority boundary is defined by a different combination, the phase set and severity basis for SF-001-PL2 would change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-PL2 severity (Catastrophic)

citations.quote: Loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case and is retained as a condition to be studied

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so passenger effects are not applicable to any SF-001 condition.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the aircraft carries flight crew only and the hold is not occupied in flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in flight, occupant effects would need assessment and could raise severities.

praData.threat: Tyre burst / flailing tread release from a main or nose gear tyre (twenty tyres total)
praData.desc: Main gear bays 710/720 each house three three-wheel bogies; nose bay 730 houses the twin-wheel nose unit. A bursting tyre releases tread/carcass fragments and pressure energy into the bay. Per §5.6.5 brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each main gear bay in adjacent bundles, separately clipped and shielded but SHARING THE BAY — a burst is a credible common cause across the two nominally independent brake supplies. Study at drawing/model stage (Figure 6-1); separation is preliminary and gear-leg/bogie count is not frozen (§1.2, App A).
praData.systems: LDG, HYD (systems A and B brake lines), FPR (gear-bay overheat detection)
praData.csfl: Tyre-burst debris confined to one main gear bay could sever or damage both the system A and system B brake lines routed through that bay (adjacent bundles, shared zone) — a single physical cause defeating the dual-hydraulic brake redundancy claimed in §5.6.2. This co-location must be reflected as a common-cause contributor in the FC-030 / FC-031 brake fault trees rather than omitted because the logical redundancy looks adequate.
praData.mitigation:
MINIMISED (subject to substantiation): SDD provides separately-clipped and shielded A/B bundles within each bay (§5.6.5), accumulator-supported emergency braking sized to six full applications with all three systems lost (§5.4.3), and steering/braking harnesses on opposite sides of each bay (§5.6.5). Whether shielding/separation survives a burst within the same bay is NOT shown at this design stage and requires trajectory/energy substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • The A/B brake hydraulic line separation within each main gear bay shall be substantiated against tyre-burst debris trajectory and energy, or the lines shall be re-routed/shielded such that a single burst cannot defeat both brake supplies
• The gear-bay overheat detection coverage shall be shown to survive a tyre-burst event or its loss shown acceptable

praData.threat: Bird strike on forward-facing structure, inlets and probes (§25.571(e)(1)/§25.631/§33.76)
praData.desc: A bird strike loads forward-facing surfaces: the nose visor structure (110, which is the pressure boundary and forward fuselage load path when closed, §5.7.1), the flight deck windshields (130), the wing leading edges (510/520, which house wing anti-ice ducting and the outboard electrical route, §5.10.5), the four engine inlets (610–640), and the ice detectors/probes/pitot-static on the forward fuselage (§5.10.2/§5.11.4). Study at drawing/model stage (Figure 6-1); geometry preliminary.
praData.systems: PRP (engine inlets), FCS/AVI (air-data probes, pitot/static/AoA), IPS (ice detectors, wing anti-ice ducting), NZD (nose visor as structure), OXY (cylinders housed in forward equipment bay 120 — see propagation)
praData.csfl: Two ice detectors are of the SAME type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (§5.10.2, commonality recorded as an item); a strike environment plus common design susceptibility is a candidate common cause for erroneous/lost ice detection. Multiple engine inlets are forward-facing across the span — a single bird is unlikely to strike more than one, but the shared inlet design is a common susceptibility to be examined. Air-data probe damage feeds erroneous air/inertial data into the FCS command path and the primary flight information (FC-071/FC-072 branches).
praData.mitigation:
SHOWN-ACCEPTABLE claim NOT yet grounded at design stage. SDD provides ice detectors on opposite sides (spatial separation, §5.10.2), standby instrument sharing no sensor/supply with primaries (§5.11.3), and engine ingestion is covered by the existing certified turbofan type (§5.1.2, §33.76 by the engine TC). Windshield and visor bird-impact capability is NOT stated in the SDD and requires §25.775/§25.631 substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • Nose visor structure and flight-deck windshields shall demonstrate bird-impact capability per §25.631/§25.775 with the pressure boundary and forward load path retained
• Air-data probe and ice-detector installation shall be shown to retain a valid, cross-checkable air-data source after a single bird strike
• Engine inlet bird-ingestion capability shall be substantiated by the engine type certificate per §33.76 for the installed configuration

praData.threat: Lightning strike (§25.581 / §25.1316, AC 20-136B) — direct-attachment and indirect-effects (induced transients on wiring)
praData.desc: Direct attachment at wing tips, nacelles, empennage, nose visor and probes, with indirect induced transients coupling onto the six EWS routes. Threat is coupling onto electrical/electronic systems via the wiring interconnection and penetration points, not just structural attachment. Survivability, not frequency: assess whether the FBW/reference/standby architecture survives a strike without common-mode defeat.
praData.systems: FCS, EPS, AVI, EWS, FPR, IPS, PRP (FADEC)
praData.csfl: A single strike inducing correlated transients on multiple EWS routes could defeat the assumed independence between the three dissimilar FCCs (three separate bays), the three ADIRUs, and the DC-essential standby instrument — the independence the FC-012/FC-018 and FC-071/FC-072 trees rely on. HV feeder left/right cross the LV signal route at two identified points in zone 300, a candidate common-coupling location.
praData.mitigation:
Bonding and lightning protection zoning of external attachment points; EWS shielding, grounding and separation (HV/LV separated throughout except two shielded crossing points in zone 300); transient-level qualification of FCC, ADIRU, standby instrument and FADEC to the induced-transient environment; standby instrument shares no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries (SDD §5.11.3) as the independent cross-check.
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft shall demonstrate that a lightning strike (direct and indirect effects) does not cause simultaneous malfunction or loss of two or more of the three flight control computers.
• The EWS shall be designed and qualified such that lightning-induced transients do not defeat the independence claimed between the three ADIRUs and the DC-essential standby instrument.
• Equipment supplied from the DC essential bus (FCC, standby instrument, fire detection, engine controls) shall be qualified to the induced-transient environment for its function level.
aiRequirements: The aircraft shall demonstrate that a lightning strike (direct and indirect effects) does not cause simultaneous malfunction or loss of two or more of the three flight control computers.
