Equipment supplied from the DC essential bus (FCC, standby instrument, fire detection, engine controls) shall be qualified to the induced-transient environment for its function level.

praData.threat: HIRF — High-Intensity Radiated Fields (§25.1317, AC 20-158A) — external RF environment coupling into electrical/electronic systems
praData.desc: External radiated RF field couples through apertures, penetrations and onto the EWS routes into the three FCC bays (fwd/mid/aft equipment bays), the ADIRUs, the display processing units, the data network and the fire-protection channels. The threat acts on every electronic function at once; survivability question is whether upset/loss of one channel correlates across the redundant set.
praData.systems: FCS, AVI, EPS, EWS, FPR, IPS
praData.csfl: An RF environment is by nature common to all channels and can therefore correlate upsets across the three dissimilar FCCs, the three ADIRUs, and the dual data networks — the same independence the FC-012 (erroneous attitude response) and FC-071/FC-072 (undetected misleading primary flight information) trees credit. Dissimilar software does not remove a shared RF coupling path.
praData.mitigation:
HIRF susceptibility qualification of FCC, ADIRU, DPU, data network and fire-detection equipment to the §25.1317 environment; EWS shielding and bundle segregation as the coupling-control means; independent standby instrument on an independent route (SDD §5.11.5) providing an out-of-band cross-check; equipment-level HIRF test evidence per AC 20-158A.
Proposed requirements: • Flight-critical equipment (FCC, ADIRU, standby instrument, FADEC, fire detection) shall be shown to perform its intended function when exposed to the HIRF environment of §25.1317.
• The design shall demonstrate that the HIRF environment does not cause correlated upset or loss across two or more of the three flight control computers or the three reference units.
• EWS shielding and segregation shall be qualified as the HIRF coupling-control means substantiating the independence claims of the affected fault trees.
aiRequirements: Flight-critical equipment (FCC, ADIRU, standby instrument, FADEC, fire detection) shall be shown to perform its intended function when exposed to the HIRF environment of §25.1317.
The design shall demonstrate that the HIRF environment does not cause correlated upset or loss across two or more of the three flight control computers or the three reference units.
EWS shielding and segregation shall be qualified as the HIRF coupling-control means substantiating the independence claims of the affected fault trees.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact (§25.571(e)(2)) — forward-facing structure and inlets
praData.desc: Hail impact on forward-facing surfaces: the nose visor (which is both structure and pressure boundary when closed), windshields, wing and stabiliser leading edges, and the four engine inlets. Model as impact energy on exposed structure and ingestion into engine inlets; the visor is a single structural load path with no redundancy. Ice-detector probes and pitot/static/AoA sensing on the forward fuselage are candidate impact targets. Installation evidence is drawing/model stage (§6 figures state topology only).
praData.systems: NZD (nose visor, pressure boundary), AVI (windshields, pitot/static/AoA, ice detectors), PRP (engine inlets), FCS (leading-edge high-lift/slats), IPS (wing/stabiliser leading edges)
praData.csfl: Common impact on forward fuselage could simultaneously affect both forward-fuselage ice detectors (recorded as same-type commonality) and multiple air-data sensing sources feeding AVI/FCS — a common-cause across nominally independent air-data channels.
praData.mitigation:
Windshield and forward-structure hail impact substantiation per §25.571(e)(2)/§25.775; engine inlet hail ingestion covered under engine type certification (§33.78); leading-edge impact resistance. Separation/shielding of the two forward-fuselage ice detectors and of pitot/static/AoA sensing so a single hail encounter does not defeat all air-data references.
Proposed requirements: • The nose visor forward structure and windshields shall withstand the certification hail impact threat without loss of pressure-boundary or structural integrity (§25.571(e)(2)).
• The two forward-fuselage ice detectors and the primary air-data sensing shall be positioned/protected so a single hail encounter cannot render all air-data references erroneous or unavailable.
aiFunctions: SF-014 Present primary flight, navigation and system information
aiRequirements: The nose visor forward structure and windshields shall withstand the certification hail impact threat without loss of pressure-boundary or structural integrity (§25.571(e)(2)).
The two forward-fuselage ice detectors and the primary air-data sensing shall be positioned/protected so a single hail encounter cannot render all air-data references erroneous or unavailable.

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and ice shedding (§25.1419, AC 20-73A)
affectedZones: forward fuselage (probes, static ports, windshields, ice detectors)
praData.desc: Ice accretion on protected surfaces if ice protection is lost or erroneously inactive, and shed-ice trajectory into downstream structure/inlets. Wing leading edges and engine cowls are bleed-heated from the shared cross-bleed manifold; stabiliser leading edges are electrically heated in six zones; probes/static ports/windshields and the two same-type ice detectors are electrically heated and individually monitored. Model each protection means separately: bleed loss vs electrical-zone loss vs probe-heat loss. Detection is by two ice detectors of the same type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage. Icing envelope to be refined to the type-design ice envelope.
praData.systems: IPS (bleed wing/cowl protection, electrical stabiliser/probe/windshield heating, two ice detectors), ECS (shared cross-bleed manifold), PRP (inlet anti-ice), AVI (probe/static/AoA sensing), FCS (leading-edge aerodynamic surfaces)
praData.csfl: The two ice detectors are identical in type — a common-mode detection failure defeats the detection redundancy; the cross-bleed manifold is a shared source such that a manifold failure removes bleed ice protection to both wings and cowls simultaneously.
praData.mitigation:
Ice protection substantiation per §25.1419 across the type-design icing envelope; annunciation of lost electrical heating zones and individually monitored probes. Dissimilarity or independent verification for ice detection given the same-type commonality (recorded item §5.10.3); bleed-source segregation so a single manifold fault does not remove all wing/cowl protection. Probe/static/windshield heat monitoring and crew alerting.
Proposed requirements: • The ice protection system shall protect the surfaces, inlets and probes required across the certification icing envelope such that loss of any single protection means or source does not produce an unsafe accretion condition (§25.1419).
• The loss of heating on any individually monitored probe, static port or ice detector shall be annunciated to the crew.
aiFunctions: SF-012 Protect wings and engine inlets from ice by bleed heating
SF-013 Protect stabilisers, probes and windshields by electrical heating
SF-014 Present primary flight, navigation and system information
aiRequirements: The ice protection system shall protect the surfaces, inlets and probes required across the certification icing envelope such that loss of any single protection means or source does not produce an unsafe accretion condition (§25.1419).
The loss of heating on any individually monitored probe, static port or ice detector shall be annunciated to the crew.

praData.threat: Cabin/cargo fire — in-flight fire or smoke originating in the unoccupied hold (stations 1–9), with smoke detection fitted but no suppression
praData.desc: Fire/smoke in the hold. Detection is at nine stations along the hold length; the SDD records that no hold suppression is fitted because the hold carries a single blade and no combustible palletised load, and that this is 'a decision somebody has to substantiate' — carried forward as an assumption. Absent suppression, an ignition source in the hold (electrical harness, restraint winch, or transiting routing) can develop unchecked. Survivability, not probability: the question is whether the aircraft survives a hold fire given detection-only, and the answer for a sustained fire cannot be shown ACCEPTABLE on the provided evidence without substantiating the no-suppression decision.
praData.systems: CRG, FPR, EWS, FUE, CRG restraint tension monitoring loop
praData.csfl: A hold fire is a single physical event that can simultaneously attack the restraint tension monitoring loop (SF-009), the low-voltage signal route and the data network channels transiting zones 200/300/400, and — via the fuel feed gallery vent shared with the hold — introduce a flammable-fluid contribution. This co-location defeats the nominal independence between payload restraint monitoring and the signal/data routes that share the hold zone; that common cause must be reflected in the affected fault trees rather than left out because the logical redundancy looks adequate.
praData.mitigation:
Detection: nine-station hold smoke detection (SF-016) provides crew annunciation. Segregation to minimise: the SDD notes the restraint tension loop shares the hold zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route, recorded as an item to examine. The absence of suppression means the residual fire cannot be ELIMINATED or MINIMISED by an installed system; the claimed outcome is therefore SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE ONLY IF the no-suppression decision is substantiated (blade non-combustibility, ignition-source elimination, and diversion/descent time). Until substantiated, a sustained hold fire is NOT shown acceptable. Candidate requirements: (a) segregate the restraint tension loop, the fuel gallery vent and the left-side LV route within the hold zone by defined minimum distance / fire barrier; (b) substantiate ignition-source elimination for hold electrical items (winches, tension loop); (c) confirm detection coverage and diversion time bound the hazard in lieu of suppression.
Proposed requirements: • The hold smoke detection coverage and annunciation shall be shown adequate to bound a hold fire to a diversion within available crew-oxygen and descent time, in lieu of installed suppression.
• The restraint tension monitoring loop, the fuel gallery vent and the left-side low-voltage route sharing the hold zone shall be segregated by defined minimum distance and/or fire barrier such that a single hold fire does not defeat their nominal independence.
• Hold electrical items (restraint winches, tension monitoring loop) shall be shown to eliminate credible ignition sources within the hold.
aiRequirements: The hold smoke detection coverage and annunciation shall be shown adequate to bound a hold fire to a diversion within available crew-oxygen and descent time, in lieu of installed suppression.

The restraint tension monitoring loop, the fuel gallery vent and the left-side low-voltage route sharing the hold zone shall be segregated by defined minimum distance and/or fire barrier such that a single hold fire does not defeat their nominal independence.
Hold electrical items (restraint winches, tension monitoring loop) shall be shown to eliminate credible ignition sources within the hold.

praData.threat: Cabin/cargo fire — in-flight fire or smoke in the flight deck / forward equipment bay (occupied compartment), including crew-oxygen cylinder involvement
praData.desc: Fire or smoke in the occupied flight deck (zone 130) or the adjacent forward equipment bay (zone 120). Zone 120 houses FCC 1, the oxygen cylinders and the forward avionics racks; zone 130 houses displays, inceptors, the standby instrument, fire handles and crew oxygen masks. A fire here directly threatens the crew and the forward flight-control and display resources, and the crew-oxygen cylinders are a stored-energy contributor. Survivability: crew smoke protection is via quick-donning full-face masks with integral smoke goggles; the standby instrument and FCC 1 are the exposed forward-bay resources.
praData.csfl: A forward-bay fire is a single event co-locating FCC 1, the forward avionics racks and the oxygen cylinders in zone 120, adjacent to the occupied flight deck. Loss of FCC 1 alone is tolerated (three dissimilar FCCs in three bays), but a zone-120 fire attacks FCC 1 together with the forward display/reference resources and the oxygen supply routed from that bay — a common cause across items whose independence rests on physical separation. This must be reflected in the FCS and display fault trees rather than assumed away.
praData.mitigation:
Detection/response: the flight deck and hold access door carry portable extinguishers; crew don quick-donning full-face masks with integral smoke goggles for smoke/fume events. Segregation to minimise: FCC 1 is one of three in three separate bays (mid and aft FCCs unaffected by a zone-120 fire); the standby instrument is wired directly to the DC essential bus on a route independent of the primary display feeders. Oxygen cylinders are installed outside the flight deck and outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source, and a thermal discharge indicator shows overboard cylinder overpressure discharge — MINIMISING the stored-energy contribution. Claimed outcome: MINIMISED for the flight-control/display effect (spatial FCC separation + independent standby) and SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE for crew survivability (smoke masks + portable extinguishers), pending confirmation of smoke evacuation and forward-bay fire containment.
Proposed requirements: • A zone-120 forward-equipment-bay fire shall not simultaneously deny FCC 1 and the independent standby instrument path; the standby instrument route independence from the forward display feeders shall be substantiated against a bay fire.
• Forward flight-deck / equipment-bay smoke protection (portable extinguishers, quick-donning masks) shall be shown to permit continued safe flight and landing through a diversion.
• Crew-oxygen cylinder installation in zone 120 shall be shown to preclude cylinder involvement in a bay fire from propagating to the occupied flight deck, with the thermal discharge indicator confirming overboard relief.
aiRequirements: A zone-120 forward-equipment-bay fire shall not simultaneously deny FCC 1 and the independent standby instrument path; the standby instrument route independence from the forward display feeders shall be substantiated against a bay fire.
Forward flight-deck / equipment-bay smoke protection (portable extinguishers, quick-donning masks) shall be shown to permit continued safe flight and landing through a diversion.

Crew-oxygen cylinder installation in zone 120 shall be shown to preclude cylinder involvement in a bay fire from propagating to the occupied flight deck, with the thermal discharge indicator confirming overboard relief.

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — pressure boundary when closed, unpressurised when open (SDD §3). Houses visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator and sensing harness; nose door lock sensing harness transits 110/120/130.
zsaData.equip: Twelve rotary latches on common torque shaft, eight locking pins, lock actuator, proximity sensing harness, mechanical indicator linkage
zsaData.interference: Common torque shaft driving all twelve latches is a single point; lock sensing harness and mechanical indicator linkage must remain independently routed (SDD §5.7.5) — co-location or shared penetration at the flight-deck bulkhead could defeat the dual-dissimilar sensing claim behind FC-042/FC-044.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify sensing harness routed opposite door actuation power and separated from indicator linkage throughout, with two separated bulkhead penetrations (§5.7.5); confirm pressure interlock (<0.1 psi) integrity; inspect torque-shaft and pin-actuator installation for maintenance-induced mis-rig.

zsaData.desc: Forward equipment bay — pressurised, conditioned (SDD §3). Houses FCC 1, oxygen cylinders and forward avionics racks; LV signal and data channel routes and the nose-door lock sensing harness transit this zone.
zsaData.equip: FCC 1, two high-pressure oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks, ADIRU (forward), LV signal harness, data network channel
zsaData.interference: High-pressure oxygen cylinders co-located with electrical/avionics racks — an oxygen-enriched atmosphere adjacent to an electrical energy source is an inherent-hazard co-location (assessed regardless of functional criticality, App K.3.1). FCC 1 is one of three separated FCC bays; loss of this bay must not couple to FCC 2/FCC 3.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm oxygen cylinder installation clear of high-energy electrical sources (§5.13.5 states cylinders are outside any zone containing a high-energy source — verify against actual bay layout); maintain FCC bay separation; inspect cylinder mounting, relief routing to the skin thermal-discharge indicator, and no chafe between LV harness and racks.

zsaData.desc: Flight deck — pressurised, occupied (SDD §3). Houses displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles and crew oxygen masks.
zsaData.equip: Four display units, two head-up displays, inceptors, integrated standby instrument, fire handles, four quick-donning oxygen masks
zsaData.interference: Standby instrument must share no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays (§5.11.3) — installation must preserve that independence behind FC-071/FC-072. Fire-handle discharge command routing to nacelles/APU must remain available; oxygen mask supply line routed clear of HV feeder (§5.13.5).
zsaData.mitigation: Verify standby instrument wired directly to DC essential bus on a route independent of primary display feeders; confirm mask supply-line separation from HV route; inspect fire-handle circuit integrity and no single-bundle common-cause between primary and standby feeds.

zsaData.desc: Forward hold stations 1-3 — low differential, unoccupied (SDD §3). Houses saddles 1-3, restraint straps, tension loop and smoke detectors; HV feeder, LV signal, data, HYD C and the restraint tension monitoring loop all transit this zone.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1-3, longitudinal restraint straps and electric winches, restraint tension monitoring loop, smoke detectors (of nine hold stations), HV feeder segment, HYD C run
zsaData.interference: Restraint tension monitoring loop is a SINGLE instrumented run sharing the hold with the fuel-gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (§5.8.5, recorded item) — a single event in this zone could defeat monitoring coverage behind the unaware restraint-degradation case (FC-050). Hold has smoke detection but NO suppression (§5.12.2) — a deliberate decision carried as an assumption to substantiate.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify tension-loop separation from fuel-gallery vent and electrical route; confirm smoke-detector coverage at all nine stations; substantiate the no-hold-suppression decision; inspect saddle hard-point pinning and strap-winch installation.

zsaData.desc: Mid hold stations 4-6 — low differential, unoccupied (SDD §3). Houses saddles 4-6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, and the HV/LV crossing points. This zone is the convergence point for the fuel cross-feed gallery, the HYD A/B shared wing-root run, HYD C, both HV feeders, both LV routes, both data channels and the cross-bleed manifold.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4-6, FCC 2, mid equipment bay, fuel cross-feed gallery, HYD A/B wing-root run, HYD C run, HV feeders left/right, LV routes, data channels, cross-bleed manifold
zsaData.interference: Highest co-location density on the aircraft. HYD A and B SHARE this wing-root run (§5.4.5, dedicated zonal item) — defeats the A/B independence claimed in FC-005/FC-017 trees; the two HV/LV crossing points (§5.5.5) are the only points HV and LV lose physical separation; the single spanwise fuel cross-feed gallery transits here (only path between sides, FC-006). FCC 2 bay must stay independent of FCC 1/FCC 3.
zsaData.mitigation: Reflect HYD A/B shared run, HV/LV crossings and single fuel gallery as explicit common-cause contributors in the affected fault trees (ARP4761A common-mode); verify shielding and minimum-distance at the two HV/LV crossings; confirm cross-bleed manifold and gallery routing separations; inspect FCC 2 bay isolation.

zsaData.desc: Aft hold stations 7-9 — low differential, unoccupied (SDD §3). Houses saddles 7-9, aft equipment bay and FCC 3; HYD C, LV signal, data channels and the restraint tension loop transit this zone.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 7-9, FCC 3, aft equipment bay, HYD C run, LV signal route, data channel, restraint tension monitoring loop segment
zsaData.interference: FCC 3 is the third of three separated FCC bays — installation must preserve independence from FCC 1 (zone 120) and FCC 2 (zone 300) behind the FC-018 complete-loss-of-attitude tree AND-gate. Restraint tension loop continues through here as a single run.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm FCC 3 bay segregation and independent DC essential feed; verify HYD C routing kept separate from A/B; inspect tension-loop continuity and saddle hard-point installation.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present (SDD §3). Houses fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting and the outboard electrical route.
zsaData.equip: Left integral fuel tanks (outboard/mid/inboard cells), cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Flammable-fluid zone with wing anti-ice hot-bleed ducting sharing the leading edge with the outboard electrical route, separated by a shielded partition (§5.10.5) — degradation of that partition is an ignition-source-to-fuel co-location. Bleed-duct overheat and any electrical arc must not reach tank vent/surge lines.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify shielded partition integrity along full anti-ice/electrical run; confirm tank vent and surge lines routed outboard of all electrical harnesses (§5.2.5); inspect for bleed-duct leak detection coverage and fuel-line/electrical minimum separation.

zsaData.desc: Left wing root — pressure boundary transit (SDD §3). Carries the HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed-duct penetration and HV feeder transit.
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run (shared), bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit
zsaData.interference: HYD A and B SHARE this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (§5.4.5, dedicated zonal item) — the recorded independence exception underpinning the FC-005/FC-017 AND-gates; co-located bleed-duct penetration adds a thermal threat to the shared hydraulic run. A single event here could take both A and B.
zsaData.mitigation: Reflect HYD A/B co-location as an explicit common-cause contributor in every tree that credits A/B independence (ARP4761A common-mode, tests every AND); verify bleed-duct penetration thermal separation from hydraulic lines; inspect pressure-boundary penetration sealing and clamping.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 (left outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (SDD §3). Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire-detection loops and extinguisher plumbing.
zsaData.equip: Turbofan engine 1, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD A), dual fire-detection loops A/B, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone with the outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm — an uncontained rotor/engine burst (applicable per §25.903(d)(1)/§25.901(c)) can release high-energy debris across the wing box, fuel gallery and adjacent HV/bleed routes. Dual fire-detection loops A/B must be routed separately with AND logic (§5.12.2).
zsaData.mitigation: Verify dual-loop separate routing and degraded single-loop logic; confirm two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair; reflect rotor-burst debris trajectory into PRA and any single-cause coupling of generator/EDP/fuel in the affected trees; inspect fire-detection loop clipping and extinguisher plumbing integrity.

zsaData.desc: Left main gear bays — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted (SDD §3). Houses three bogies, brake lines A and B, and steering/brake harnesses.
zsaData.equip: Three three-wheel bogies, brake hydraulic lines A and B, anti-skid units, steering and brake electrical harnesses, gear-bay overheat detection
zsaData.interference: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through the bay in ADJACENT bundles, separately clipped and shielded but sharing the bay (§5.6.5, recorded zonal item) — a single bay event (tyre burst, brake fire, overheat) could take both A and B braking supplies behind FC-030. Tyre burst / flailing tread is an applicable particular risk (§25.734).
zsaData.mitigation: Reflect A/B brake-line co-location as a common-cause contributor in the complete-loss-of-braking tree (ARP4761A common-mode); verify shielding and separate clipping; confirm gear-bay overheat detection coverage; inspect for tyre-burst debris shielding of brake lines and harnesses.

zsaData.desc: Aft fuselage and empennage — mixed environment, APU compartment is a fire zone (SDD §3). Houses rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders and the APU compartment.
zsaData.equip: Upper and lower rudder segment control runs, stabiliser (electrical) heater feeders, APU, APU generator, APU dedicated extinguisher bottle, APU dual fire-detection loops
zsaData.interference: Rudder upper and lower segment runs are routed on opposite sides of the aft fuselage (§5.3.5) and the split-rudder arrangement is the directional-control sizing case (FC-005/FC-018) — installation must preserve segment independence. APU is a designated fire zone co-located with rudder runs and stabiliser feeders; an APU fire must not propagate to both rudder segment runs.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify rudder upper/lower segment runs remain on opposite sides with no shared penetration; confirm stabiliser heater feeders routed opposite the rudder runs (§5.10.5); confirm APU dual-loop detection, automatic shutdown/fuel isolation and dedicated bottle; inspect APU fire-zone boundary integrity relative to control runs.

cmaData.subject: G-001 Fuel starvation to affected-side engine (FC-005) — independence of the three fuel-supply loss inputs (both collector boost pumps, gravity feed path, cross-feed)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The three fuel-supply paths to an engine fail independently.. Loss of thrust on one side via fuel starvation requires simultaneous loss of both collector boost pumps AND unavailability of gravity feed AND unavailability of cross-feed to the affected-side engine (AND gate, node id 6).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / Environment concerns defeating parts of the claim: (1) Cross-feed is a SINGLE spanwise gallery through the wing box — the only path from one side to the opposite engines — so the cross-feed input is itself a single point, not a redundant path; a gallery fault removes it for all engines simultaneously. (2) The gallery transits zone 300 alongside the HYD A/B run, both HV feeders and the cross-bleed manifold, so a zone-300 particular risk or fire couples the cross-feed input with wider damage. (3) Both collector boost pumps per engine are AC-driven from the electrical resource (EPS); a common AC-supply loss to that collector defeats the 'both boost pumps' branch as a shared-resource common cause rather than two independent pump failures. (4) Gravity feed is only available below FL150 — the gravity-path input is unavailable by design in cruise, so the AND gate collapses toward two inputs at altitude.
cmaData.mitigation: Model the single cross-feed gallery as a common-cause / single-point contributor rather than an independent AND input; add the shared-AC-supply-to-collector coupling as a common-cause event on the 'both boost pumps failed' branch; qualify the gravity-feed input with a flight-phase (altitude) condition. Substantiate gallery routing separation via PRA/ZSA on zone 300.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The three fuel-supply paths to an engine fail independently.

cmaData.subject: G-004 FC-005 top event — independence between [loss/reduction of thrust on one side] AND [directional-control authority not available]
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The thrust-loss cause and the directional-control-authority loss are independent.. FC-005 (partial thrust loss with asymmetry beyond available directional control) requires an affected-side thrust loss AND coincident loss of directional-control authority (AND gate, node id 1).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / Installation concerns: (1) The rudder actuation that provides directional authority is supplied by HYD A and HYD B; HYD A is pumped off engines 1&2 and HYD B off engines 3&4 — so an outboard-engine thrust loss and a same-side rudder-supply degradation can share the same engine as a common cause, coupling the two AND inputs. (2) The directional-control input draws on the HYD A/B shared wing-root run through zone 300/530 (recorded installation item where A and B share a run); a zone event there degrades rudder authority while an asymmetric thrust event is present. (3) Electrical power to FADEC (thrust side) and to actuator control electronics (rudder side) both stem from the EPS resource; a shared bus loss can contribute to both inputs. The directional-control sizing case is explicitly an outboard-engine failure at V1 with max blade payload, so thrust-loss and authority-loss are physically correlated at the sizing condition, not independent.
cmaData.mitigation: Represent the engine-driven-pump coupling (engine loss → same-side HYD source degradation → rudder authority) as an explicit common-cause contributor rather than an independent AND; carry the HYD A/B shared wing-root run (zone 530/300) as a zonal common-cause item; verify rudder split-segment supply (A upper, B lower) preserves authority under single-side HYD loss.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The thrust-loss cause and the directional-control-authority loss are independent.

cmaData.subject: G-009 Independent loss of all four engines (FC-006) — independence of the four engine-loss inputs
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The four engines fail independently — no single shared cause disables the redundant set of four.. Complete loss of propulsive thrust via independent engine loss requires simultaneous independent loss of engines 1, 2, 3 and 4 (AND gate, node id 14).
cmaData.findings: Common Design / Common Resource / Environment concerns that defeat the four-way independence: (1) COMMON ENGINE TYPE — a single existing certified turbofan of the 330 kN class in all four positions; a common design/material deficiency or a fleet-wide type issue is a common cause across all four (SDD flags reliability data as assumption). (2) COMMON FADEC DESIGN — each engine's dual-channel FADEC is the same design across all four engines; a common software/design fault is a common cause. (3) COMMON FUEL — all four fed from the fuel resource (FUE); common fuel contamination / a single cross-feed gallery is already captured as a separate OR input to FC-006 (node 31) and must not be double-counted here but confirms fuel is a shared resource. (4) The FADEC channels are stated to take power from four different sources so that no single bus loss affects more than one engine — that mitigates the electrical-supply common cause and should be verified, not assumed. Engines 1/2 sit in left zones and 3/4 in right zones, giving physical separation against a single zonal event, but a common bleed cross-manifold and common fuel remain shared resources.
cmaData.mitigation: Add explicit common-cause contributors for (a) common engine type design/material deficiency and (b) common FADEC design fault, combined with the independent four-way failure logic, rather than leaving a falsely optimistic four-input AND. Keep common fuel contamination in the separate FC-006 OR branch (do not double-count). Verify the 'four different power sources for FADEC' claim as an independence requirement; substantiate engine model reliability once the type is released to engineering.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The four engines fail independently — no single shared cause disables the redundant set of four.

cmaData.subject: G-012 pitch FCC channel independence (nodes 37 AND 38): erroneous pitch command generation vs cross-channel voting/monitor trap
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three dissimilar flight control computers and of the command-vs-monitor functions within the FBW command path for pitch.. The FCC channel producing an erroneous pitch surface command and the cross-channel voting/monitor that should trap it fail independently, so an erroneous pitch command reaching the elevators/THS requires two independent failures.
cmaData.findings: Common software/specification: SDD §5.3.2 hosts FCC software developed by only two teams under a dissimilarity argument for three channels, so a specification-level error in the common pitch control law or in the voting/monitor logic is not covered by the two-team split and can corrupt both the erroneous-command leg and the trap leg together. Common input: all channels vote on shared ADIRU air-data/inertial data (node 56 on this tree), so a common erroneous reference biases every channel identically and the monitor sees agreement, defeating the AND. Common environment/co-location: FCC 1/2/3 in zones 120/300/400; zone 300 is the convergence point for HV/LV crossing, cross-feed gallery, HYD A/B run and data channels (SDD §3, §4), a candidate zonal common cause for FCC 2. The command generation and the cross-channel monitor are logically related functions; a shared monitor specification error is a single cause affecting both AND inputs.
cmaData.mitigation:
Three physically separated equipment bays and opposite-side dual network routing (SDD §5.3.5, §5.11.5); dissimilar software teams (SDD §5.3.2); cross-channel voting; independent standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing (SDD §5.11.3). Not yet assured: three-channel dissimilarity from a two-team split, and independence of the monitor function from the command function.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS shall demonstrate that the cross-channel voting/monitor function is specified and implemented independently of the pitch command-generation function such that no single specification or software error disables both.
• The FCS shall substantiate that a two-team software dissimilarity argument provides adequate independence across three flight control computers, or provide additional dissimilarity/monitoring for the pitch axis.
• The FCS shall demonstrate that a common erroneous air-data/inertial reference cannot produce an undetected erroneous pitch command through cross-channel agreement.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-built: independent development of command vs monitor (DO-178C dissimilarity/independence argument), zonal analysis of FCC 2 in zone 300 convergence, and ADIRU common-mode monitoring. Close each independence requirement with evidence.

cmaData.subject: G-019 FCC channel uncommanded PITCH output vs cross-channel monitor — independence of command lane and detection
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Command-channel fault and its cross-channel monitor are independent — no single shared cause disables both the generating channel and the detection that would inhibit its uncommanded output.. The FCC channel generating an uncommanded pitch surface output and the cross-channel voting/monitor that should detect/inhibit it fail independently (AND-gate node 59).
cmaData.findings: Common-design coupling: FCS software developed by only TWO teams across THREE FCCs under a dissimilarity argument (SDD §5.3.2), so at least two channels share a software team — a common software error can produce the same uncommanded pitch output AND defeat the like-coded monitor in the paired channel. Common installation/environment: although FCC 1/2/3 are in three separate bays (SDD §5.3.5), all three command/monitor data paths converge in zone 300 (mid hold, HV/LV crossing points, FCC 2 co-located; zonal model), a single-zone event able to strike command and monitor together. Shared-sensor input: erroneous air-data/inertial reference feeds all channels (tree nodes 55/56 context), coupling the command source and the comparison basis. Intra-channel command-vs-monitor partitioning is NOT described in the SDD — independence of the monitor from the generating lane inside a single FCC is unverified.
cmaData.mitigation:
Substantiate three-way, not two-way, software dissimilarity across the pitch command and monitor lanes, or demonstrate the two-team coding cannot produce a coincident undetected uncommanded output; ZSA of zone 300 to show a single mid-hold event cannot take command and monitor paths together; independent air-data/inertial source assignment for the monitor comparison; DO-178C DAL A partitioning evidence that the intra-channel monitor is independent of the commanding lane.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS shall demonstrate that the cross-channel monitor detecting an uncommanded pitch surface command is not disabled by any single software error shared with the commanding channel (three-way dissimilarity or equivalent argument).
• The FCS installation shall demonstrate by zonal analysis that no single event in zone 300 defeats both an FCC command path and its cross-channel monitor for the pitch axis.

cmaData.subject: Independence of the three flight control computers — FC-017 partial-attitude-loss AND (2-of-3 FCC degraded command)
cmaData.claim: The three FCCs fail independently, so a degraded/erroneous command requires two independent channel faults (AND at node 92).
cmaData.findings: Common software/development: SDD §5.3.2 states three dissimilar computers host software developed by only TWO teams under a dissimilarity argument — three channels on two software baselines means at least two channels share a code base, defeating full three-way independence for a common software fault. Common data source: all three FCCs consume the same air-data/inertial reference set (three ADIRUs, SDD §5.11.2) and pilot inceptor position; a common erroneous reference drives all channels alike (this is why the FC-016 tree already carries an 'Erroneous air-data/inertial data' contributor). Physical co-location/routing: FCC 2 is in zone 300, the convergence zone for both HV feeders, both LV routes and both data channels; a zone-300 event can strike FCC 2's supply and signalling in common. Common part/manufacturing across the three computers is not stated as dissimilar hardware.
cmaData.mitigation:
Add a common-software basic event across the two-team-shared channels (or a common-cause gate) under node 92; add a common erroneous air-data/inertial reference contributor as a repeated event feeding the FCC channels; confirm the third FCC is on the independent software team and record the software dissimilarity partition; assess zone 300 (PRA/ZSA) for a single event defeating FCC 2 plus its routing.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS shall implement software dissimilarity such that no single software fault degrades more than one of the three FCC command channels.
• The FCS shall ensure the three FCC channels use monitored/voted air-data and inertial references such that a single erroneous reference cannot drive a common degraded command.
aiRequirements: The FCS shall implement software dissimilarity such that no single software fault degrades more than one of the three FCC command channels.
The FCS shall ensure the three FCC channels use monitored/voted air-data and inertial references such that a single erroneous reference cannot drive a common degraded command.

cmaData.subject: Independence of the three FBW command paths — FC-018 'Loss of all fly-by-wire command paths' AND (all three FCCs)
cmaData.claim: All three FCC command paths fail independently, so complete loss of FBW command requires three independent path losses (AND at node 96).
cmaData.findings: Common electrical resource: SDD §5.5.2 makes the DC essential bus the aircraft's final electrical resort supplying the flight control computers; loss of the DC essential bus removes the essential-supplied channel and is a shared upstream feed across FBW paths — a repeated/common-cause event rather than three independent losses. Physical separation is strong: the three FCCs are in three separate bays (120/300/400, SDD §5.3.5) and rudder runs are on opposite sides. Residual co-location: the mid equipment bay (zone 300) houses FCC 2 and is the convergence point for both HV feeders, both LV routes and both data channels, so a zone-300 particular risk can couple FCC 2 loss with the routing feeding the other channels. Common software (two teams across three computers, §5.3.2) can also produce a coincident command-path fault.
cmaData.mitigation:
Add the DC essential bus as a repeated event / common-cause contributor across the three FBW-path branches under node 96; verify each FCC is fed from a genuinely different electrical source per §5.5.2 and that no two share the DC essential feed; run a zone-300 ZSA and the applicable PRAs (rotor burst, HIRF, lightning) against the FCC-2 + routing convergence; carry the two-team software dissimilarity as a common-cause item.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The EPS shall supply the three FCC command paths from independent sources such that loss of the DC essential bus does not remove more than one FBW command path.
• The installation shall ensure no single zonal event in zone 300 defeats more than one FCC command path together with its power and signal routing.
aiRequirements: The EPS shall supply the three FCC command paths from independent sources such that loss of the DC essential bus does not remove more than one FBW command path.
The installation shall ensure no single zonal event in zone 300 defeats more than one FCC command path together with its power and signal routing.

cmaData.subject: Independence of FBW command loss vs mechanical reversion — FC-018 top AND (complete loss of attitude control)
cmaData.claim: Complete loss of attitude control requires loss of all FBW command paths AND loss of the mechanical reversion path together (top AND at node 95).
cmaData.findings: Design diversity present: the mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment (SDD §5.3.2) is dissimilar from the electrical FBW paths, which supports independence of the two AND inputs. Residual couplings: the mechanical reversion path acts on the stabiliser trim and the LOWER rudder segment, whose actuation is supplied by hydraulic systems (elevators from A/C, lower rudder from B) — a hydraulic common cause (e.g. HYD A/B shared wing-root run in zone 530/300, SDD §5.4.5) can degrade both the FBW-driven surfaces and the surfaces the mechanical path relies on. Physical convergence in zone 300/530 (shared HYD A/B run plus FCC 2) is a candidate common environment defeating the AND. The mechanical path is described as a single path (no redundancy in the reversion itself).
cmaData.mitigation:
Test the top AND against a common hydraulic cause: verify the mechanical reversion path's stabiliser-trim and lower-rudder actuation do not depend on the same hydraulic system(s) whose loss also fails the FBW branch; assess the HYD A/B shared wing-root run (zone 530/300) as a common-cause defeating this AND; add a hydraulic-common-cause contributor if the reversion actuation shares a system with an FBW branch; confirm the mechanical linkage routing is segregated from the FCC bays.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS mechanical reversion path shall not share a hydraulic system or a physical zone whose single loss also fails all three FBW command paths.
• The installation shall segregate the mechanical reversion linkage from the FCC command routing such that no single zonal event fails both AND inputs.
aiRequirements: The FCS mechanical reversion path shall not share a hydraulic system or a physical zone whose single loss also fails all three FBW command paths.
The installation shall segregate the mechanical reversion linkage from the FCC command routing such that no single zonal event fails both AND inputs.

cmaData.subject: G-035/G-037 — Loss of all hydraulic motive power to the wheel brakes (node 104: HYD B normal AND HYD A alternate AND accumulator reserve)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of HYD A, HYD B and the brake accumulator supplying wheel braking. The normal (HYD B), alternate (HYD A) and accumulator-reserve brake supplies fail independently, so complete loss of wheel-braking requires all three.
cmaData.findings:
Table M2 — Independence Principle: HYD A / HYD B / accumulator independence for wheel braking.
[Installation Design] Concern: HYD A and HYD B share a wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (zones 530/300) | Effect: a single localised event at the shared run can degrade both A and B, defeating the A-alternate/B-normal AND | Mitigating factor / lack of independence: SDD records the shared run as a dedicated zonal item; separate clipping claimed but co-location remains — NOT independent at the wing-root.
[Installation Design / Environment] Concern: brake hydraulic lines A and B run through each main gear bay (zones 710/720) in adjacent, separately-clipped bundles | Effect: a gear-bay event (tyre burst per §25.734, overheat, wheel-brake fire) strikes both A and B lines together | Mitigating factor: adjacent-but-separately-clipped and shielded per SDD §5.6.5; reconcile with tyre-burst PRA and 710/720 zonal overheat item — co-location is a residual common cause.
[Common Resources] Concern: HYD C does not supply the brakes, so the brake AND rests only on A, B and the accumulator — no third independent hydraulic source | Effect: narrows the independence set to two hydraulic systems that already share routing | Mitigating factor: accumulator reserve sized to six full applications is genuinely independent of pumping/routing and is the strongest leg of the AND.

cmaData.subject: G-061 APU compartment dual-loop fire/overheat detection independence (loop A AND loop B)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual continuous detection loops per zone with AND-warning logic, routed separately and separately clipped (SDD §5.12.2, §5.12.5).. The APU dual-loop detection AND asserts detection loop A and detection loop B fail independently, so simultaneous loss of both is remote.
cmaData.findings: Common design: both loops are the same continuous detection loop type installed in the same APU compartment (zone 800), so a single detection-technology or lot defect is a common-cause contributor. Common environment: the APU compartment is a fire zone — a fire/overheat/mechanical event in zone 800 can strike both separately-clipped loops together, defeating the physical separation the AND relies on. Common resource: both loops are supplied from the DC essential bus (SDD §5.12.4) — loss of that bus removes both loops (already an OR contributor at node 183, not inside this AND). Common maintenance: same loop type invites a common calibration/installation error across both.
cmaData.mitigation:
Loops routed on opposite sides of the zone and separately clipped (SDD §5.12.5). Confirm dissimilar routing survives a credible zone-800 fire/thermal event per ZSA; consider dissimilar loop technology or lot separation to break the common-design coupling; verify DC-essential-bus dependency is modelled outside the AND (it is, at node 183).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two APU-compartment detection loops shall be substantiated as surviving independently a credible fire/overheat event within zone 800 (ZSA).
• The two APU-compartment detection loops shall be procured/installed such that a single manufacturing lot or calibration action cannot disable both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA/ZSA to confirm loop-A/loop-B physical and environmental independence in zone 800 and that the DC-essential-bus common supply is captured outside this AND.

cmaData.subject: G-062 Complete loss of fire, overheat and smoke detection — cross-zone detection independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent detection per zone: dual-loop nacelle/APU detection, bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat detection, and nine-station hold smoke detection (SDD §5.12.2).. The complete-loss-of-detection AND asserts nacelle, APU, bleed-duct, gear-bay and hold detection are independent, so total loss requires all to fail together.
cmaData.findings: Common resource: every detection channel — nacelle, APU, bleed-duct overheat, gear-bay overheat and hold smoke — is supplied from the DC essential bus (SDD §5.12.4), so a single DC-essential-bus loss defeats the entire AND at once. This is the dominant common cause and is correctly drawn as an OR contributor at node 183 rather than left inside the parallel logic. Common design: nacelle and APU dual loops share loop type (see G-061), and the two ice-detector-style commonalities do not apply here. Common environment: detection zones are physically dispersed (nacelles 610-640, APU 800, gear bays 710/720, hold 200-400), so no single zonal event strikes all — physical independence across zones holds.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain DC essential bus as an explicit shared-resource contributor (node 183) outside the AND — the AND overstates protection if that supply is treated as independent. Confirm zonal dispersion defeats any single-zone particular risk; no additional physical common cause identified across the dispersed detection zones.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The complete-loss-of-detection fault tree shall model the DC essential bus supply to fire detection as a single shared-resource contributor, not as an independent parallel branch.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA to confirm the DC-essential-bus contributor is modelled outside the detection AND and that no single zonal/particular risk strikes all dispersed detection zones.

cmaData.subject: G-065 Both cross-plumbed engine-pair extinguisher bottles fail to deliver agent
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair (SDD §5.12.2).. The both-bottles AND asserts bottle 1 and bottle 2 of a cross-plumbed engine pair fail to discharge independently, so failure of both is remote.
cmaData.findings: Common resource: both bottles' discharge circuits are supplied from the hot battery bus (SDD §5.12.4) — loss of that supply defeats both discharge paths, and it is drawn as an OR contributor at node 187, outside this AND. Common resource / single path: the cross-plumbing / distribution path is shared between the two bottles for a given nacelle (nodes 192/196) — a blocked or ruptured cross-plumb defeats both bottles into that nacelle, so the AND is not fully independent at its plumbing. Common design: both bottles are the same type/charge, so a common agent-charge-loss mechanism (leakage, temperature) or a common squib/valve lot defect can affect both (nodes 190/191, 194/195). Common maintenance: same bottle type invites a common servicing/charge error across the pair. Common environment: both bottles serve a fire zone — a nacelle/pylon fire could compromise shared plumbing before discharge.
cmaData.mitigation:
Cross-plumbing gives coverage of either nacelle but is itself a shared path — capture it as a common-cause contributor (already at nodes 192/196). Retain hot-battery-bus supply as a shared-resource contributor (node 187). Consider lot separation / staggered charge inspection between the two bottles to break the common agent-charge and squib-lot coupling; verify shared plumbing survives a credible nacelle fire.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two bottles of each engine pair shall be substantiated against a common agent-charge-loss and a common squib/discharge-valve lot defect (dissimilar lot or staggered inspection).
• The shared cross-plumbing distribution path shall be modelled as a common-cause contributor and substantiated as surviving a credible nacelle fire prior to discharge.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA to confirm the hot-battery-bus supply and the shared cross-plumbing path are modelled outside the two-bottle AND, and that common bottle charge/squib defects are addressed.

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the uncommanded thrust change from the engine-parameter indication and asymmetry cues, identify it as an uncommanded thrust variation on the affected engine(s), and counter it with rudder and thrust-lever inputs.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-001 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect that the thrust response does not match the commanded thrust from engine indication and aircraft response, identify the erroneous response, and re-command thrust to obtain the intended result.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-002 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the thrust asymmetry from directional cues and engine indication, identify the affected engine, secure it via the fuel shut-off and fire handle, and manage a continued-flight or diversion while countering asymmetry with rudder.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-004 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The analysis assumes the crew cannot arrest the resulting heading/roll divergence with the remaining directional-control authority, so the condition is not recoverable by crew action near the ground.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-005 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The analysis assumes the crew cannot recover propulsive thrust and is relied upon only to carry the workload of conducting an unpowered forced landing, the outcome of which depends on altitude and available landing site.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-006 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the sudden asymmetric thrust/drag event from directional cues and engine indication, identify the in-flight reverser deployment, and counter it with rudder and thrust management.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-007 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the induced yaw from directional cues during rollout, identify the asymmetric reverser condition, and counter it with nose-wheel steering, rudder and differential braking.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-008 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the reduced deceleration from rollout progression and indication, and respond by applying increased wheel braking while monitoring remaining rollout margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-009 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the absence of reverse deceleration and respond by decelerating on wheel braking alone while monitoring the reduced rollout margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-010 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect that the attitude response does not match the command from attitude display and aircraft behaviour, identify the discrepancy, and attempt recovery through the degraded or reversion control paths.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-012 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the unexpected attitude excursion from the attitude display and motion cues, arrest it, and re-establish the intended attitude with the remaining control authority.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-013 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded control law and reduced or lost envelope protection from the alerting/annunciation, and fly within a restricted manoeuvre envelope while carrying the elevated workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-016 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The analysis assumes the crew cannot arrest the divergence with the remaining attitude-control authority regardless of workload, so the condition is not recoverable by crew action.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-017 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The analysis assumes the crew has no effective means to control attitude, so the condition is not recoverable by crew action.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-018 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the rolling moment from lateral-control demand and configuration indication, identify the asymmetric high-lift condition, and counter it with lateral control while flying an approach and landing in that configuration.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-019 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the unexpected configuration change from high-lift position indication and aircraft response, identify the uncommanded movement, and respond to the out-of-schedule performance.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-020 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the loss of high-lift capability from configuration indication, and fly a higher-speed approach and landing while assessing go-around and diversion options.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-021 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the reduced flap/slat availability from configuration indication, and reassess reference speed and landing distance for the degraded configuration while carrying the increased workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-022 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded ground roll/taxi behaviour and manage it with increased directional-control input on the unmaintained surface, carrying the elevated workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-026 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded ground directional control and stopping performance and manage the aircraft on the unmaintained surface, carrying the elevated workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-027 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The analysis assumes the crew cannot arrest or control the aircraft on the ground by any means once ground support is lost, so the condition is not recoverable by crew action.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-028 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect that braking is not honouring the command from deceleration cues and aircraft behaviour, identify the erroneous braking, and counter it while maintaining directional control on the unmaintained surface.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-029 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the loss of normal wheel braking from deceleration cues and indication, and respond by reverting to reverse thrust and accumulator emergency braking while managing the potential overrun.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-030 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded stopping performance from deceleration cues, and respond by applying maximum braking and reverse thrust while monitoring remaining distance.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-031 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the induced yaw from directional cues during deceleration, identify the asymmetric braking, and maintain runway track with steering and rudder inputs.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-032 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to perceive the directional deviation from heading cues, identify the erroneous steering response, and correct it with rudder pedals, differential braking and reverse.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-035 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the unexpected yaw/heading change from directional cues, identify the uncommanded nose-wheel deflection, and counter it with pedals and differential braking.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-036 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the reduced steering authority from steering response and heading cues, and supplement directional control with rudder and differential braking during ground manoeuvring.
